title: From Local GEBV to a Crossing Decision: Haplotype-Based Parent Selection
text: Sections 3-7 answer “parents.” stop short “crossed ” — select_parents_ga()/truncation_selection()/ select_parents_by_family() return flat set notion pairing. usefulness_criterion() (Usefulness Criterion / UC, Schnell & Utz 1975; Bernardo 2003; Zhong & Jannink 2007) picks ranks candidate crosses, candidate parents, predicted quality best progeny cross plausibly produce — takes whichever three shortlists (parent list ) hand parent_ids, preference one origin another (see Section 5.5): UC=μmid-parent+⋅σcross2UC = \mu_{\text{mid-parent}} + \cdot \sqrt{\sigma^2_{\text{cross}}} – mid-parent value plus selection-intensity-scaled term cross’s predicted genetic variance. high-UC cross need high-merit parents sides; cross strong parent complementary weaker--different one can -rank two mediocre--similar strong parents, predicted segregate better best-progeny tail. Four variance-prediction modes trade data requirements rigor (see ?usefulness_criterion full detail): reach . founder/parent shortlist (Sections 5.1/5.2, list built way), usefulness_criterion() tool next question : “keep,” “pairs actually cross.” particularly worth running programme capacity make limited number biparental crosses per cycle wants prioritise ones likely segregate genuinely better best-progeny tail, just ones two highest-ranked individuals; suspect complementary--moderate pairing might -perform two similar elite parents cross, e.g. two parents carry different favourable haplotypes blocks rather one. skip . need parent list, cross list – stop Section 5, adds nothing . need actual contribution numbers full mating plan balanced across whole set crosses , population-wide inbreeding explicit cap, tool either — UC ranks candidate cross independently notion others, exactly gap Section 9 closes next. practice, choosing variance_model. Match mode data already rather reaching rigorous one default: "block_independent" needs nothing beyond Step 1 already produced, ’s right default starting point panels; "phased" worth extra phasing step within-block gametic detail actually changes ranking (check comparing two modes’ top crosses , rather assuming); "linked" next step "phased" also genetic map suspect target blocks close enough together treating independent ("phased" ) real concern — extra package needed, just computation (Monte Carlo); "simplemating" worth extra data requirements (0/2-coded DH/RIL genotypes, genetic map) specifically need multi-generation RIL/DH population variance , just single cross’s F1-style segregation variance. block-independent mode reuses exactly Section 3 already computed — new model fit needed: selected_proportion fraction cross’s progeny actually keep making (drives selection-intensity term ); set whatever programme’s realistic within-cross selection pressure . Passing n_progeny (real, finite biparental population size, e.g. 200) switches asymptotic Falconer & Mackay (1996) formula exact finite-population Monte Carlo estimate — asymptotic formula overstates intensity small crosses, matters realistic biparental population sizes. re-ranks 20 GA-selected parents cross potential rather individual merit. Worth checking directly: highest-UC cross actually pair two highest-merit parents, something complementary? top-ranked cross’s parents simply two highest-GEBV individuals shortlist, UC job: predicting complementary pairing segregate better best-progeny tail mid-parent value alone suggest. Like Section 5, usefulness_criterion() still decide many progeny advance cross manage population-wide inbreeding – Section 9’s job.

title: Introduction to HapBlockR
text: HapBlockR detects linkage disequilibrium (LD) blocks genome-wide SNP data extends pipeline haplotype reconstruction, diversity analysis, genomic prediction feature engineering. Two LD metrics available: Standard r² – fast, kinship correction, suitable 10 M+ markers unstructured populations. Kinship-adjusted rV² – corrects relatedness-induced LD inflation, livestock, inbred lines, family-based cohorts. See LD Metrics vignette statistical detail decision table. C++/Armadillo computational core makes algorithm approximately 40x faster original Big-LD implementation typical window sizes. vignette covers complete pipeline – reading genotype data, block detection, haplotype analysis, parameter tuning – using ldx_geno example dataset (120 individuals, 230 SNPs, 3 chromosomes, 9 simulated LD blocks). Everything builds toward breeding decision: block detection defines units haplotype analysis operates , haplotype analysis turns units per-block genetic values, Section 13.5 shows first step turning ranked list candidates. full path actual selected set parents – GA-based parent selection truncation-selection baseline, family/diversity checks, forward-simulated genetic gain – see Local GEBV Crossing Decision vignette.

text: original Big_LD() calls cor() inside boundary-scan loop per CLQD() call, matrix operations running R interpreter. WGS rice panel 3 million SNPs across 12 chromosomes, original implementation take days workstation. HapBlockR replaces critical paths eight compiled C++ functions:

title: Introduction to HapBlockR
text: score_favorable_haplotypes() summarize_parent_haplotypes() rank candidates inventory favourable alleles. stop ranked list – turning actual set parents (GA-optimised coverage important blocks, checked truncation-selection baseline, family-balance diagnostics, forward-simulated genetic gain) covered Local GEBV Crossing Decision vignette.
code: pred <- run_haplotype_prediction(   geno_matrix = ldx_geno, snp_info = ldx_snp_info, blocks = blocks,   blues = blues_vec, verbose = FALSE ) ae <- decompose_block_effects(   haplotypes = haps, snp_info = ldx_snp_info,   blocks = blocks, snp_effects = pred$snp_effects[[1]] ) scores <- score_favorable_haplotypes(haps, allele_effects = ae, normalize = TRUE) head(scores[, c("id","stacking_index","n_blocks_scored","rank")], 10) top10  <- scores$id[scores$rank <= 10] inv    <- summarize_parent_haplotypes(haps, candidate_ids = top10,                                        allele_effects = ae, min_freq = 0.02) inv[inv$dosage > 0 & inv$is_rare & !is.na(inv$allele_effect) & inv$allele_effect > 0,     c("id","block_id","allele","dosage","allele_freq","allele_effect")]

what: 13.6 Haplotype association testing with simpleM correction
title: Introduction to HapBlockR
text: test_block_haplotypes() uses unified Q+K mixed linear model. simpleM procedure (Gao et al. 2008, 2010, 2011) estimates effective number independent tests (Meff) eigenspectrum haplotype allele dosage correlation matrix, providing family-wise error control less conservative raw Bonferroni. estimate_diplotype_effects() now supports correction set test_block_haplotypes(). five p-value columns always present $omnibus_tests; sig_metric controls drives significant flag:
code: blues_vec <- setNames(ldx_blues$YLD, ldx_blues$id)  # EMMAX with FDR — recommended for discovery assoc_fdr <- test_block_haplotypes(   haplotypes = haps,   blues      = blues_vec,   blocks     = blocks,   n_pcs      = 0L,   sig_metric = "p_fdr",   verbose    = FALSE ) cat("Significant (FDR <= 0.05):", sum(assoc_fdr$allele_tests$significant), "\n")  # Q+K with simpleM Šidák — recommended for family-wise error control assoc_sm <- test_block_haplotypes(   haplotypes       = haps,   blues            = blues_vec,   blocks           = blocks,   n_pcs            = 3L,                 # Q+K model (used when optimize_pcs = FALSE)   sig_metric       = "p_simplem_sidak",  # simpleM Šidák correction   meff_scope       = "chromosome",       # recommended: separate Meff per chr   meff_percent_cut = 0.995,              # 99.5% variance threshold (Gao default)   verbose          = FALSE )  # Per-chromosome Meff assoc_sm$meff$trait$allele$chromosome  # All four p-value columns always present regardless of sig_metric # p_wald | p_fdr | p_simplem | p_simplem_sidak | Meff | alpha_simplem | ... head(assoc_sm$allele_tests[order(assoc_sm$allele_tests$p_wald),                             c("block_id","allele","effect","SE",                               "p_wald","p_simplem","p_simplem_sidak","Meff")], 5)  # Automatic PC selection — let the data choose n_pcs via BIC/lambda hybrid # Recommended when lambda_GC is far from 1.0 with a fixed n_pcs. assoc_opt <- test_block_haplotypes(   haplotypes       = haps,   blues            = blues_vec,   blocks           = blocks,   optimize_pcs     = TRUE,              # triggers BIC/lambda model selection   optimize_pcs_max = 10L,              # test k = 0..10   optimize_method  = "bic_lambda",     # recommended: |lambda-1| + 0.01*BIC   sig_metric       = "p_simplem_sidak",   meff_scope       = "chromosome",   plot             = TRUE,             # saves PDF plots including pca_grm.pdf   out_dir          = "results",        # and grm_scree.pdf   verbose          = TRUE )  # Inspect selection table print(assoc_opt$pc_model_selection) #  n_pcs     BIC lambda_gc  score selected #      0  1234.1     1.021 0.0210    FALSE #      1  1231.5     1.015 0.0150    FALSE #      2  1230.8     1.003 0.0033    FALSE #      3  1232.1     0.999 0.0011     TRUE   <-- selected  # Multi-trait: all traits share the same GRM assoc_mt <- test_block_haplotypes(   haplotypes = haps,   blues      = ldx_blues,   blocks     = blocks,   id_col     = "id",   blue_cols  = c("YLD", "RES"),   n_pcs      = 3L,   sig_metric = "p_simplem_sidak",   verbose    = FALSE ) dip <- estimate_diplotype_effects(   haplotypes       = haps,   blues            = blues_vec,   blocks           = blocks,   min_n_diplotype  = 3L,   sig_metric       = "p_omnibus_simplem_sidak",  # recommended   meff_percent_cut = 0.995,   verbose          = FALSE )  # All five columns always present: # p_omnibus_adj | p_omnibus_fdr | p_omnibus_simplem | p_omnibus_simplem_sidak | Meff head(dip$omnibus_tests[, c("block_id","trait","F_stat","p_omnibus",                             "p_omnibus_fdr","p_omnibus_simplem_sidak",                             "Meff","significant")], 5)  # Blocks showing overdominance (heterosis candidates) dip$dominance_table[dip$dominance_table$overdominance,                     c("block_id","allele_A","allele_B","a","d","d_over_a")]

title: Introduction to HapBlockR
text: compare_block_effects() validates whether haplotype effects one population replicate another. computes IVW meta-analytic effects, Cochran Q heterogeneity (tests whether effect sizes differ populations), ² inconsistency, direction agreement per block. Key distinction: boundary_overlap_ratio output column automatically computed block tables supply — set . boundary_overlap_warn input parameter (default 0.80) controls boundary_warning = TRUE raised output. Interpreting output:
code: # Best practice: use Pop A's block boundaries for Pop B to maximise # shared alleles and ensure haplotype strings are directly comparable. haps_B_harm <- harmonize_haplotypes(   extract_haplotypes(geno_B, snp_info, blocks_A),  # same block coordinates   reference = haps_A )  assoc_A <- test_block_haplotypes(haps_A, blues = blues_A, blocks = blocks_A,                                   sig_metric = "p_simplem_sidak") assoc_B <- test_block_haplotypes(haps_B_harm, blues = blues_B, blocks = blocks_A,                                   sig_metric = "p_simplem_sidak")  # block_match = "id" (default): match by block_id string # block_match = "position": match by genomic IoU -- use when blocks differ conc <- compare_block_effects(   assoc_A, assoc_B,   pop1_name             = "PopA",   pop2_name             = "PopB",   blocks_pop1           = blocks_A,   blocks_pop2           = blocks_B,   # Pop B own block table (may differ)   block_match           = "position", # recommended when blocks not identical   overlap_min           = 0.50,   direction_threshold   = 0.75,   boundary_overlap_warn = 0.80 )  # $concordance — one row per block: IVW effect, Q_stat, I2, replicated, ... conc$concordance[conc$concordance$replicated,                  c("block_id","n_shared_alleles","direction_agreement",                    "meta_p","Q_p","I2","replicated")]  # $shared_alleles — per-allele IVW detail head(conc$shared_alleles[, c("block_id","allele","effect_pop1","effect_pop2",                                "direction_agree","ivw_effect","ivw_SE")])  print(conc)   # summary: n blocks compared, n replicated, median I²

title: Introduction to HapBlockR
text: GWAS run outside HapBlockR, use compare_gwas_effects(). accepts either output define_qtl_regions() (recommended, auditable) raw GWAS data frames plus block tables (convenience path). Note external GWAS provides one lead SNP per block (multiple haplotype alleles), effect_correlation Cochran Q always NA. Replication judged direction agreement meta_p ≤ 0.05.
code: # Path 1: pre-mapped (recommended) # define_qtl_regions() maps each marker to its LD block and identifies # the lead SNP (smallest p-value) as the block representative. qtl_A <- define_qtl_regions(gwas_A, blocks, snp_info, p_threshold = 5e-8) qtl_B <- define_qtl_regions(gwas_B, blocks, snp_info, p_threshold = 5e-8)  conc_gwas <- compare_gwas_effects(   qtl_pop1    = qtl_A,   qtl_pop2    = qtl_B,   blocks_pop1 = blocks_A,   blocks_pop2 = blocks_B,   block_match = "position",   overlap_min = 0.50,   pop1_name   = "PopA",   pop2_name   = "PopB" )  # Path 2: raw GWAS + blocks (calls define_qtl_regions internally) # When SE is absent, it is derived from BETA and P via z-score. # Column names are flexible: use beta_col, se_col, p_col arguments. conc_raw <- compare_gwas_effects(   gwas_pop1     = gwas_A,   gwas_pop2     = gwas_B,   blocks_pop1   = blocks,   blocks_pop2   = blocks,   snp_info_pop1 = snp_info,   # snp_info_pop2 reuses this when NULL (shared panel)   pop1_name     = "PopA",   pop2_name     = "PopB",   p_threshold   = 5e-8,   beta_col      = "BETA",     # change if named differently in your GWAS output   se_col        = "SE",       # NULL or absent: derived from z-score automatically   p_col         = "P" )  # Same output class as compare_block_effects() # Extra columns: lead_marker_pop1/pop2, lead_p_pop1/pop2, #                se_derived_pop1/pop2, both_pleiotropic conc_gwas$concordance[conc_gwas$concordance$replicated, ] print(conc_gwas)

title: Introduction to HapBlockR
text: HapBlockR v0.3.1 adds three epistasis functions operate GRM-corrected REML residuals null model test_block_haplotypes(). Within-block SNP interaction scan (scan_block_epistasis): tests C(p,2) SNP pairs inside significant blocks interaction term aaij y = mu + aixi + ajxj + aaij(xixj) + e. Corrected Bonferroni simpleM Sidak within block; sig_metric controls drives significant flag. -block trans-haplotype scan (scan_block_by_block_epistasis): tests significant haplotype alleles every allele blocks. Identifies genetic background dependence haplotype resolution — form epistasis single-block single-SNP analyses detect. Single-block fine-mapping (fine_map_epistasis_block): identifies specific interacting SNP pair within block. Auto-dispatches exhaustive pairwise scan (p <= 200 SNPs) LASSO interaction terms (p > 200 SNPs). Statistical note. n=204 individuals Bonferroni correction ~300,000 within-block pairs, detection threshold approximately p < 1.7 × 10^-7 per block. Power detect pairwise SNP epistasis threshold low unless interaction effect large (|aa| > ~0.3 SD). -block trans-haplotype scan better powered haplotype dosage column aggregates multi-SNP variation, reducing effective number tests increasing signal--noise ratio per test.
code: # Within-block epistasis (restricted to significant_omnibus blocks) epi_within <- scan_block_epistasis(   assoc              = assoc,   geno_matrix        = res$geno_matrix,   snp_info           = snp_info,   blocks             = blocks,   blues              = blues_list,   haplotypes         = haps,   trait              = "BL",   sig_metric         = "p_simplem_sidak",   max_snps_per_block = 300L ) print(epi_within) epi_within$results[epi_within$results$significant, ]  # Between-block trans-haplotype epistasis epi_between <- scan_block_by_block_epistasis(   assoc      = assoc,   haplotypes = haps,   blues      = blues_list,   blocks     = blocks,   trait      = "BL" ) print(epi_between)  # Fine-map a single block # y_resid must be pre-computed from the REML null model fine <- fine_map_epistasis_block(   block_id    = "block_12_1054210_1086071",   geno_matrix = res$geno_matrix,   snp_info    = snp_info,   blocks      = blocks,   y_resid     = my_reml_residuals,   method      = "auto" ) head(fine)

what: 1. The kinship problem in LD estimation
title: LD Metrics: Standard r² and Kinship-Adjusted rV²
text: standard squared Pearson correlation two SNP (Single Nucleotide Polymorphism) dosage vectors gjg_j gkg_k : rjk2=[Cov(gj,gk)Var(gj)Var(gk)]2r^2_{jk} = \left[\frac{\mathrm{Cov}(g_j, g_k)}   {\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(g_j)\,\mathrm{Var}(g_k)}}\right]^2 estimator assumes nn individuals drawn independently population. structured related populations fails: two individuals sharing recent common ancestor carry correlated alleles loci, just loci true LD. sample covariance picks genuine LD kinship-induced allele sharing, inflating r2r^2 causing blocks drawn broadly.

title: LD Metrics: Standard r² and Kinship-Adjusted rV²
text: Mangin et al. (2012) proposed kinship-adjusted squared correlation: rVjk2=[Cor(V−1/2gj,V−1/2gk)]2rV^2_{jk} = \left[\mathrm{Cor}(V^{-1/2} g_j,\; V^{-1/2} g_k)\right]^2 V=ZZ⊤/(2∑jpjqj)V = ZZ^\top / (2\sum_j p_j q_j) VanRaden (2008) genomic relationship matrix (GRM) V−1/2V^{-1/2} inverse square root. Left-multiplying V−1/2V^{-1/2} removes kinship-induced correlation resulting correlation measures recombination-based LD.

code: set.seed(1) G_small <- ldx_geno[, 1:30] Gc      <- scale(G_small, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE) V_demo  <- tcrossprod(Gc) / 30 + diag(0.05, nrow(Gc))  A_chol <- get_V_inv_sqrt(V_demo, method = "chol") A_eig  <- get_V_inv_sqrt(V_demo, method = "eigen")  max(abs(A_chol %*% V_demo %*% t(A_chol) - diag(120))) #> [1] 80.21798 max(abs(A_eig  %*% V_demo %*% t(A_eig)  - diag(120))) #> [1] 4.574119e-14

title: Statistical Phasing with Beagle 5.x in HapBlockR
text: extract_haplotypes() default mode produces diploid allele strings — concatenation individual’s allele codes (0, 1, 2) every Single Nucleotide Polymorphism (SNP) block. Within high-linkage disequilibrium (LD) block strings nearly 1:1 true haplotype classes (Calus et al. 2008) sufficient diversity analyses genomic prediction tasks. However, several analyses require knowledge alleles reside chromosome (gametic phase): True gametic haplotype dosage: counting many copies haplotype allele individual carries separate chromosomes (0, 1, 2) rather whether combined diploid string matches pattern. Inbreeding estimation: fine-scale runs homozygosity require gametic phasing. Heterosis modelling: identifying heterozygous diplotypes unambiguously. Forward-simulating crossing decision: ga_vs_ts_simulation() compares genetic algorithm (GA)-selected truncation-selected founders simulated generations, needs know alleles cis simulate recombination respects LD blocks founders selected – see Local GEBV Crossing Decision vignette comparison Section “Reading pre-phased VCF” getting hap1/hap2 function. HapBlockR provides true statistical phasing via Beagle 5.x integration run_ldx_pipeline(phase = TRUE).

title: Statistical Phasing with Beagle 5.x in HapBlockR
text: Calling run_ldx_pipeline(phase = TRUE) triggers following sequence, transparently within pipeline: LD block detection runs unphased dosage matrix (correct LD computation — phasing change allele correlations). Beagle phasing called original VCF via phase_with_beagle(). phased VCF written out_prefix.vcf.gz out_dir. Phased VCF reading via read_phased_vcf() parses 0|1 GT fields three matrices: hap1 (gamete 1), hap2 (gamete 2), dosage =    hap1 + hap2. Sample SNP alignment aligns phased data cleaned/imputed marker set using composite key (CHR + POS + REF + ALT + SNP ID). robust VCF--VCF minor header differences. Bigmemory caching (use_bigmemory = TRUE): hap1, hap2, dosage written three binary-backed matrices bigmemory_path. next run bigmemory_path unchanged phased VCF, pipeline reattaches disk instantly without re-reading VCF re-running Beagle. Phased haplotype extraction passes list(hap1, hap2, dosage) extract_haplotypes(), produces gametic allele strings (g1|g2) per block per individual.

what: Q+K model with simpleM correction (recommended for family-wise control)
title: HapBlockR Workflow: From Genotype File to Haplotype Features
text: Use sig_metric = "p_simplem_sidak" meff_scope = "chromosome" want family-wise error control accounts correlation among haplotype alleles (less conservative raw Bonferroni). four p-value columns always present output regardless sig_metric.
code: assoc_sm <- test_block_haplotypes(   haplotypes       = haps,   blues            = blues_vec,   blocks           = blocks,   n_pcs            = 3L,                 # Q+K: 3 GRM-derived PCs as fixed effects   sig_metric       = "p_simplem_sidak",  # simpleM Šidák (recommended)   meff_scope       = "chromosome",       # separate Meff per chromosome (recommended)   meff_percent_cut = 0.995,              # 99.5% variance threshold (Gao default)   verbose          = FALSE )  # Per-chromosome effective test counts assoc_sm$meff$YLD$allele$chromosome  # All four p-value columns always present names(assoc_sm$allele_tests) # ... "p_wald" "p_fdr" "p_simplem" "p_simplem_sidak" "Meff" ...

title: HapBlockR Workflow: From Genotype File to Haplotype Features
text: compare_block_effects() validates whether haplotype effects discovered one population replicate another, using IVW meta-analysis, Cochran Q heterogeneity, direction agreement:
code: # Assumes assoc_popA and assoc_popB are test_block_haplotypes() results # from two independent populations, both run using the same block boundaries  conc <- compare_block_effects(   assoc_pop1            = assoc_popA,   assoc_pop2            = assoc_popB,   pop1_name             = "PopA",   pop2_name             = "PopB",   blocks_pop1           = blocks_popA,   blocks_pop2           = blocks_popB, # Pop B own block table (may differ)   block_match           = "position",  # match by genomic IoU; match_type column reports result   overlap_min           = 0.50,   # min IoU for 'position' match (else 'pop1_only')   direction_threshold   = 0.75,   boundary_overlap_warn = 0.80 )  # boundary_overlap_ratio is an OUTPUT column (automatically computed from block # tables); boundary_overlap_warn is the INPUT threshold (default 0.80) that # controls when boundary_warning = TRUE is set.  # Replicated blocks: directionally concordant AND Q_p > 0.05 conc$concordance[conc$concordance$replicated, ]  # Per-allele IVW detail head(conc$shared_alleles)  print(conc)   # summary: n compared, n replicated, median I²

text: Within-block -block epistasis functions operate GRM-corrected REML residuals null model test_block_haplotypes(), ensuring population-structure-corrected tests throughout.

title: HapBlockR Workflow: From Genotype File to Haplotype Features
code: # Scan all C(p,2) SNP pairs within significant blocks # Tests H0: aa_ij = 0  in  y = mu + ai*xi + aj*xj + aa_ij*(xi*xj) + e # Corrected by Bonferroni AND simpleM Sidak within each block epi_within <- scan_block_epistasis(   assoc              = assoc,          # test_block_haplotypes() result   geno_matrix        = geno_matrix,   snp_info           = snp_info,   blocks             = blocks,   blues              = blues,   haplotypes         = haps,   trait              = "YLD",   sig_blocks         = NULL,           # uses significant_omnibus blocks   max_snps_per_block = 300L,           # exhaustive up to 300 SNPs/block   sig_metric         = "p_simplem_sidak",   sig_threshold      = 0.05 )  # Output: class HapBlockR_epistasis print(epi_within)  # Significant interacting pairs epi_within$results[epi_within$results$significant, ]  # Per-block summary: n_snps, n_pairs, n_significant, min_p epi_within$scan_summary  # All correction columns always present # p_wald | p_bonf | p_simplem | p_simplem_sidak | Meff # significant | significant_bonf | significant_simplem | significant_simplem_sidak

code: # Tests significant haplotype alleles x all other blocks # O(n_sig x n_total_alleles) tests -- tractable at WGS scale # Identifies genetic background dependence: a haplotype at block A # only functions in the presence of a specific haplotype at block B epi_between <- scan_block_by_block_epistasis(   assoc      = assoc,   haplotypes = haps,   blues      = blues,   blocks     = blocks,   trait      = "YLD",   sig_alleles = NULL,    # NULL = uses significant alleles from assoc   sig_threshold = 0.05 )  print(epi_between) epi_between$results[epi_between$results$significant, ]  # Results columns: # block_i, allele_i, block_j, allele_j, CHR_i, CHR_j, same_chr # aa_effect, SE, t_stat, p_wald, p_bonf, significant

title: HapBlockR Workflow: From Genotype File to Haplotype Features
text: Statistical note. typical WGS sample sizes (n < 300), detection threshold within-block Bonferroni correction C(p,2) pairs stringent. -block trans-haplotype scan better powered haplotype dosage column aggregates multi-SNP variation, providing stronger signal--noise ratio per test.
code: # Fine-map specific interacting SNP pairs within one block. # Requires pre-computed REML residuals from the null model. # method = "auto": pairwise scan for p <= 200 SNPs, LASSO for larger blocks.  # Pre-compute residuals (example using the null model from test_block_haplotypes) feat <- build_haplotype_feature_matrix(haps, min_freq = 0.05,                                         encoding = "additive_012")$matrix G_grm <- compute_haplotype_grm(feat) common <- intersect(rownames(G_grm), names(blues)) y  <- blues[common] fit <- rrBLUP::mixed.solve(y = y, K = G_grm[common, common], method = "REML") y_resid <- y - as.numeric(fit$beta) - fit$u[common]  # Exhaustive pairwise scan for blocks with <= 200 SNPs fine <- fine_map_epistasis_block(   block_id    = "block_12_1054210_1086071",   geno_matrix = geno_matrix,   snp_info    = snp_info,   blocks      = blocks,   y_resid     = y_resid,   method      = "auto"   # pairwise <= 200 SNPs, lasso otherwise ) head(fine)  # Columns (pairwise): SNP_i, SNP_j, POS_i, POS_j, dist_bp, #                     aa_effect, SE, t_stat, p_wald, p_bonf, significant # Columns (lasso):   SNP_i, SNP_j, POS_i, POS_j, dist_bp, lasso_coef, selected

title: HapBlockR -- Genome-Wide LD Block Detection
text: Genomic selection tells breeder good candidate . , rarely tells specific parents cross, whether favourable genetics carry actually complementary set, whether choice outperform simply taking top-ranked individuals. Answering questions means going one level single breeding value — haplotype blocks actually driving — searching founder set jointly covers favourable blocks, rather eyeballing ranked list. Closing gap HapBlockR’s breeding decision layer built . short: decomposes breeding value already (GBLUP (Genomic Best Linear Unbiased Prediction)/mixed-model workflow) block level, searches founder set best covers important blocks real crossing-scheme constraints, benchmarks founder set truncation-selection baseline, carries forward ranked list crosses full contribution--mating plan. Section 2 breaks every function layer — block-level GEBV (Genomic Estimated Breeding Value) decomposition Optimal Contribution Selection — full. See Local GEBV Crossing Decision vignette worked example, start finish: breeding value crossing block mating plan. Reaching decision reliably still depends block detection underneath correct population hand, LD block detection remains foundational step modern genomic analyses. Knowing SNPs (Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms) co-segregate unit determines GWAS (Genome-Wide Association Study) results interpreted, haplotypes defined population genetics, genomic prediction models structured. Despite importance, implementations LD block detection suffer three problems limit usefulness practice. kinship problem. Classical LD estimators (r²) assume independence individuals. livestock, crop, family-based human cohorts assumption systematically violated. Cryptic relatedness inflates pairwise correlations, causing LD appear stronger blocks drawn broadly wrong places. kinship-adjusted squared correlation rV² (Mangin et al. 2012, Heredity 108:285-291) corrects whitening genotype matrix inverse square root genomic relationship matrix (GRM): Xᵛ = V⁻¹⁄² G̃ kinship-whitened, mean-centred genotype matrix; V = ZZᵀ / (2 Σⱼ pⱼqⱼ) VanRaden (2008) GRM; V⁻¹⁄² inverse square root. scale problem. original Big-LD implementation (Kim et al. 2018) contains compiled code. modern whole-genome sequencing panels 2-10 million markers inner loops prohibitively slow, loading full genotype matrix detection impossible workstations. HapBlockR addresses C++/Armadillo computational core compiled via Rcpp, OpenMP-parallelised LD computation, unified multi-format /O layer, strict never-full-genome memory model. pipeline gap. original Big-LD stops block boundaries. HapBlockR adds complete downstream pipeline: statistical phasing via Beagle 5.x bigmemory-backed caching, haplotype extraction, diversity metrics, genomic prediction features, association testing, breeding decision tools.
code: rV²ᵢⱼ = Cov(Xᵛᵢ, Xᵛⱼ)² / [Var(Xᵛᵢ) · Var(Xᵛⱼ)]

title: HapBlockR -- Genome-Wide LD Block Detection
text: HapBlockR takes genotyped panel breeding value already (GBLUP/mixed-model workflow) specific, defensible set parents next crossing cycle — just LD block table. extends Big-LD algorithm Kim et al. (2018) breeding decision layer built top substantially re-engineered detection core. Breeding decision layer — see Local GEBV Crossing Decision vignette full worked example: Local GEBV per haplotype block — run_haplotype_prediction() (Tong et al. 2025) decomposes breeding value per-block contributions, breeder can see comes , just much . Block-importance triage — select_top_blocks() plot_block_funnel() separate small set blocks driving variance rest. GA-based parent selection — select_parents_ga() searches founder set jointly covers favourable blocks, five real crossing-scheme constraints (no_selfing/selfing/OHS/OPV/ Haploid_OHS), benchmarked truncation_selection() baseline. Optional merit_weight rewards whole-genome merit directly inside search (GA+TS hybrid), guarding selecting noisy per-block estimates. Don’t want guess raw multiplier? Set merit_priority instead — plain 0-100 “much care merit vs. coverage” dial, auto-calibrated data (call suggest_merit_weight() first see calibration numbers committing one). Optional coancestry_weight/G penalise relatedness directly inside search ; target_degree easier alternative — 0-90 dial select_parents_ocs() uses, converted relatedness ceiling data rather raw penalty multiplier. Family-quota parent selection — select_parents_by_family() picks best-performing families (, via group_by = "genetic_cluster", data-derived genetic clusters) first, best lines within , enforcing group balance directly selection rule. Family ranking shrinkage-corrected default (small families pulled toward pack rather trusted raw sample mean alone — see NEWS.md breaking-change note); optional relatedness ceiling (within_group_target_degree) balances score diversity within group; optional cross-family haplotype-diversity check (coverage-gain default, original dominant-block heuristic) discourages picking representatives different groups genomically redundant. Forward-simulation proof genetic gain — ga_vs_ts_simulation() plot_ga_vs_ts_simulation() simulate recurrent selection generations founder sets, GA’s answer can checked naive one rather taken faith. Diversity family-balance diagnostics — plot_parent_selection_pca() shows selection sits population’s genetic diversity; pairing pedigree/family table catches -represented family crosses made. Cross ranking true Optimal Contribution Selection (OCS) — usefulness_criterion() ranks candidate crosses predicted mid-parent value plus segregation variance (Schnell & Utz 1975; Bernardo 2003), four variance-prediction modes: unphased block-independent, exact phased 4-gamete, native Monte Carlo linkage-aware mode (variance_model =   "linked", extra dependency), genuine multi-locus, linkage-aware mode via SimpleMating::getUsefA() (Peixoto et al. 2024). select_parents_ocs() solves classical Meuwissen (1997) contribution- optimisation problem via two true-OCS engines (AlphaMate executable, optiSel’s candes()/opticont()/matings() solver, Wellmann 2019), producing actual contribution--mating plan population- wide relatedness explicit cap; third engine (SimpleMating’s planCross()/selectCrosses()) instead discrete greedy cross prediction/selection — different algorithm class, useful want fast candidate-pair screening rather solved contribution optimum. Explicit tradeoffs validation — select_parents_pareto() sweeps merit-vs-relatedness tradeoff visible Pareto frontier instead one scalar dial; validate_crosses_exact() checks heuristic mating plan true optimum via exact integer linear programming; select_core_collection() covers reverse case representing genetic diversity objective (genebank/reference-panel curation), via classical farthest-point maximin heuristic. Haplotype stacking association tools — score_favorable_haplotypes(), summarize_parent_haplotypes(), test_block_haplotypes(), estimate_diplotype_effects() round inference layer feeding breeding decisions. Detection computation layer — 15 core improvements original Big-LD implementation make layer possible genome-wide scale: Dual LD metric — standard r² (default) kinship-adjusted rV² C++/Armadillo core — thirteen compiled functions handle expensive operations OpenMP parallelism — outer loop compute_r2_cpp() parallelised Unified multi-format /O — numeric CSV, HapMap, VCF/VCF.gz, GDS, PLINK BED, R matrix Never-full-genome memory model — genome never held RAM format MAF filter C++ — single O(np) pass NA imputation C++ boundary scan — replaces R inner loop subsegmentation Sparse r² computation — O(p) cost large sub-segments Automatic parameter tuning — tune_LD_params() grid search Haplotype reconstruction — phase-free Beagle-phased pathways Diversity metrics — richness, , Shannon entropy, dominant haplotype frequency Prediction feature matrix — multi-locus dosage columns GBLUP/BayesB/ML Polynomial community detection — Louvain Leiden WGS panels Sparse LD computation — max_bp_distance restricts pairs physical window Memory-mapped genotype store — read_geno_bigmemory() OS-page access

title: HapBlockR -- Genome-Wide LD Block Detection
text: test_block_haplotypes() uses unified Q+K mixed linear model simpleM multiple-testing correction (Gao et al. 2008, 2010, 2011). model jointly corrects population structure polygenic kinship: y = μ + α · x_hap + Σ β_k · PC_k + g + ε, g ~ MVN(0, σ²_g G) Key parameters: n_pcs = 0L (default, EMMAX): GRM random effect absorbs structure n_pcs = k: top-k GRM eigenvectors additional fixed effects (Q+K model) n_pcs = NULL: auto-selected GRM scree-plot elbow optimize_pcs = FALSE: TRUE, auto-selects n_pcs fitting null models k = 0..optimize_pcs_max minimising criterion set optimize_method. principled elbow heuristic GWAS. optimize_pcs_max = 10L: maximum PCs evaluated optimize_pcs = TRUE "bic" — minimise BIC null REML model "lambda" — minimise |λ_GC − 1| (genomic control calibration) "bic_lambda" (default, recommended) — hybrid: |λ−1| + 0.01·scaled_BIC. Minimises inflation/deflation BIC breaks ties toward fewer PCs "p_wald" — raw Wald p-value (use pre-corrected threshold) "p_fdr" — Benjamini-Hochberg FDR (recommended discovery) "p_simplem" — simpleM Bonferroni-style: min(p × Meff, 1) "p_simplem_sidak" — simpleM Šidák-style: 1−(1−p)^Meff (recommended correlated haplotype predictors) "chromosome" (recommended) — separate Meff per chromosome "global" — one genome-wide Meff "block" — one Meff per LD block (omnibus tests get Meff = 1) meff_percent_cut: variance threshold simpleM eigendecomposition (default 0.995) plot = TRUE: saves PDF plots (PNG). Three files per run: manhattan_<trait>.pdf, qq_<trait>.pdf, pca_grm.pdf (GRM PCA coloured phenotype), grm_scree.pdf (eigenvalue scree selected PC red) four p-value columns (p_wald, p_fdr, p_simplem, p_simplem_sidak) always present every output regardless sig_metric. estimate_diplotype_effects() also now supports full correction set new sig_metric parameter. four p-value columns (p_omnibus_adj, p_omnibus_fdr, p_omnibus_simplem, p_omnibus_simplem_sidak) always present $omnibus_tests regardless chosen sig_metric. estimate_diplotype_effects() decomposes variation block additive () dominance (d) components. Dominance ratio d/classifies gene action: 0 = additive, ±1 = complete dominance, |d/| > 1 = overdominance.
code: # FDR-based discovery (EMMAX, default) assoc_fdr <- test_block_haplotypes(   haps, blues = blues_vec, blocks = blocks,   sig_metric = "p_fdr", verbose = FALSE )  # simpleM Šidák with Q+K correction, chromosome-wise Meff assoc_sm <- test_block_haplotypes(   haps, blues = blues_vec, blocks = blocks,   n_pcs            = 3L,   sig_metric       = "p_simplem_sidak",   meff_scope       = "chromosome",   meff_percent_cut = 0.995,   verbose          = FALSE ) assoc_sm$meff$trait$allele$chromosome   # per-chromosome effective test counts head(assoc_sm$block_tests[order(assoc_sm$block_tests$p_omnibus), ])

title: HapBlockR -- Genome-Wide LD Block Detection
text: compare_block_effects() takes two test_block_haplotypes() result objects independent populations computes per-block statistics quantifying consistently haplotype allele effects replicate across panels. Key output columns (one row per block per trait):
code: # Use Pop A's block boundaries for Pop B (maximises shared alleles) haps_B_harm <- harmonize_haplotypes(   extract_haplotypes(geno_B, snp_info, blocks_A),   # same block coords   reference = haps_A ) assoc_A <- test_block_haplotypes(haps_A, blues = blues_A, blocks = blocks_A,                                   sig_metric = "p_simplem_sidak") assoc_B <- test_block_haplotypes(haps_B_harm, blues = blues_B, blocks = blocks_A,                                   sig_metric = "p_simplem_sidak")  # block_match = "id" (default): match by block_id string — fast, backward-compatible # block_match = "position":      match by genomic interval overlap — handles different #                                 LD block boundaries between populations conc <- compare_block_effects(   assoc_A, assoc_B,   pop1_name             = "PopA",   pop2_name             = "PopB",   blocks_pop1           = blocks_A,   # required for boundary_overlap_ratio + position matching   blocks_pop2           = blocks_B,   # supply Pop B's OWN block table (may differ from A)   block_match           = "position", # recommended when blocks differ between populations   overlap_min           = 0.50,       # min IoU for two blocks to be considered the same region   direction_threshold   = 0.75,   boundary_overlap_warn = 0.80 ) # $concordance$match_type: "exact" | "position" | "pop1_only" # "position" rows: same QTL region, different boundary definitions conc$concordance[conc$concordance$replicated, ]   # replicated blocks head(conc$shared_alleles)                          # per-allele IVW detail print(conc)

title: HapBlockR -- Genome-Wide LD Block Detection
text: GWAS run externally (GAPIT, TASSEL, FarmCPU, PLINK, tool), compare_gwas_effects() compares block-level lead-SNP effects two populations. accepts either raw GWAS data frames pre-mapped output define_qtl_regions(). Key differences compare_block_effects(): SE derivation. Many GWAS tools omit standard error. SE absent, compare_gwas_effects() derives z-score: SE = |BETA| / |z|, z = Φ⁻¹(P/2). se_derived_pop1 / se_derived_pop2 output columns flag population required derivation. Shared marker panel. populations genotyped array sequenced reference, set snp_info_pop2 = NULL (default) reuse snp_info_pop1. populations different marker sets, supply snp_info_pop2 explicitly.
code: # Path 1: pre-mapped (recommended) — most auditable qtl_A <- define_qtl_regions(gwas_A, blocks, snp_info, p_threshold = 5e-8) qtl_B <- define_qtl_regions(gwas_B, blocks, snp_info, p_threshold = 5e-8)  conc <- compare_gwas_effects(   qtl_pop1      = qtl_A,   qtl_pop2      = qtl_B,   blocks_pop1   = blocks_A,       # Pop A's block table   blocks_pop2   = blocks_B,       # Pop B's block table (may differ from A)   block_match   = "position",     # match by genomic overlap — handles different boundaries   overlap_min   = 0.50,           # min IoU for a valid match   pop1_name     = "PopA",   pop2_name     = "PopB" )  # Path 2: raw GWAS + blocks (convenience — calls define_qtl_regions internally) conc2 <- compare_gwas_effects(   gwas_pop1     = gwas_A,   gwas_pop2     = gwas_B,   blocks_pop1   = blocks_A,   blocks_pop2   = blocks_B,   snp_info_pop1 = snp_info,   # snp_info_pop2 = NULL: reuses snp_info_pop1 when marker panels are shared   pop1_name     = "PopA",   pop2_name     = "PopB",   block_match   = "position",  # match blocks by genomic interval overlap   overlap_min   = 0.50,        # blocks with IoU < 0.5 become "pop1_only"   p_threshold   = 5e-8,   beta_col      = "BETA",      # column name — change to match your GWAS tool   se_col        = "SE",        # NULL or absent: derived from z-score automatically   p_col         = "P" )  # Output uses the same HapBlockR_effect_concordance class # GWAS-specific extra columns in $concordance: #   lead_snp_pop1, lead_snp_pop2  — which SNP tagged the block in each pop #   lead_p_pop1, lead_p_pop2      — lead SNP p-values #   se_derived_pop1/pop2          — TRUE when SE was derived from z-score #   both_pleiotropic              — TRUE when block is pleiotropic in both pops conc$concordance[conc$concordance$replicated, ] print(conc)

title: HapBlockR -- Genome-Wide LD Block Detection
text: HapBlockR provides three functions epistasis detection extend haplotype association framework. operate GRM-corrected REML residuals null model test_block_haplotypes(), ensuring population-structure-corrected tests throughout. scan_block_epistasis() tests C(p,2) SNP pairs within significant block pairwise interaction GRM-corrected REML residuals. model pair : y = μ + aᵢxᵢ + aⱼxⱼ + aaᵢⱼ(xᵢ × xⱼ) + ε Restricting significant blocks avoids genome-wide explosion: 15 significant blocks ~200 SNPs , total number tests ~300,000 rather ~4.4 billion. Multiple testing corrected Bonferroni simpleM Sidak within block, Meff estimated eigenspectrum pairwise interaction column matrix. scan_block_by_block_epistasis() trans-haplotype epistasis scan tests significant haplotype allele every allele blocks. conceptually analogous trans-eQTL scan phenotypic haplotype interactions — detects genetic background dependence resistance haplotype one locus functions presence specific background another locus. 25 significant alleles × 17,943 total alleles, scan involves ~450,000 tests corrected Bonferroni. fine_map_epistasis_block() fine-maps single block identifying specific interacting SNP pairs. blocks p ≤ 200 SNPs runs exhaustive pairwise scan. larger blocks uses LASSO pairwise interaction terms (glmnet::cv.glmnet(), lambda.1se), avoids multiple-testing burden identifying influential pairs.
code: # Within-block epistasis scan (significant blocks only) epi_within <- scan_block_epistasis(   assoc              = assoc,          # test_block_haplotypes() result   geno_matrix        = res$geno_matrix,   snp_info           = snp_info,   blocks             = blocks,   blues              = blues_list,   haplotypes         = haps,   trait              = "BL",   sig_blocks         = NULL,           # NULL = use significant_omnibus blocks   max_snps_per_block = 300L,   sig_metric         = "p_simplem_sidak",   sig_threshold      = 0.05 ) print(epi_within) epi_within$results[epi_within$results$significant, ] epi_within$scan_summary  # Between-block trans-haplotype epistasis scan epi_between <- scan_block_by_block_epistasis(   assoc         = assoc,   haplotypes    = haps,   blues         = blues_list,   blocks        = blocks,   trait         = "BL",   sig_alleles   = NULL,    # NULL = significant alleles from assoc   sig_threshold = 0.05 ) print(epi_between) epi_between$results[epi_between$results$significant, ]  # Fine-map a single block (auto-dispatches: pairwise or LASSO) fine <- fine_map_epistasis_block(   block_id   = "block_12_1054210_1086071",   geno_matrix = res$geno_matrix,   snp_info    = snp_info,   blocks      = blocks,   y_resid     = my_reml_residuals,   # from .fit_null_reml() or null model   method      = "auto",              # pairwise <= 200 SNPs, lasso otherwise   sig_threshold = 0.05 ) head(fine)

title: Clique-Based LD Block Detection — CLQD
text: Partitions SNPs genomic window LD cliques. Three algorithms available via CLQmode: "Density" (default) Standard Big-LD clique scoring – edges     built full r? matrix, cliques found Bron-Kerbosch     (igraph::max_cliques), scored density = size / span.     Exact, exponential worst-case. Use checkLargest = TRUE     guard blowup dense WGS panels. "Maximal" algorithm Density scored clique     size (original Big-LD maximality criterion). "Louvain" Louvain community detection     (igraph::cluster_louvain). Polynomial time O(n log n) – never     exponential. Recommended WGS panels (>500 SNPs per window)     time CLQmode = "Density" slow. Communities returned     bin IDs matching Density output format downstream code     unaffected. "Leiden" Leiden community detection     (igraph::cluster_leiden). Stricter Louvain – produces     well-connected communities without disconnected nodes. Requires     igraph >= 1.3.0. Slightly slower Louvain higher quality     communities. Recommended Louvain resolution matters. max_bp_distance supplied (> 0), SNP pairs within physical distance r? computed (compute_r2_sparse_cpp). reduces O(p?) LD computation near-O(p) WGS panels long-range LD negligible (typically > 500 kb). Applied clique algorithm.

title: Cross-Population Haplotype Effect Concordance — compare_block_effects
text: Given two allele_tests data frames produced test_block_haplotypes two independent populations, computes per-block (optionally per-trait) statistics quantify consistently haplotype allele effects replicate across populations. Statistics computed per block: Effect correlation (\(r\)) Pearson correlation per-allele     effect sizes populations across shared alleles. Requires     least 3 shared alleles; NA otherwise. Direction agreement Proportion shared alleles     populations assign sign effect. value >= 0.75     (.e. least 3 4 alleles agree direction) considered     strong directional replication. Inverse-variance weighted (IVW) meta-analytic effect weighted     mean effect \(\hat\beta_{\mathrm{IVW}} = \sum w_i \beta_i /     \sum w_i\) \(w_i = 1/\mathrm{SE}_i^2\).  Computed separately     shared allele summarised mean per-allele IVW     estimates. IVW meta-analysis framework used     two-sample Mendelian randomisation cross-population GWAS     meta-analysis (see Borenstein et al. 2009). Cochran's Q heterogeneity statistic Tests whether effect sizes     differ significantly two populations:     \(Q = \sum w_i (\beta_i - \hat\beta_{\mathrm{IVW}})^2\).     null heterogeneity, \(Q \sim \chi^2_{n-1}\).     Significant Q (large \(Q_p\)) indicates effect sizes differ     populations - sign GxE interaction, LD structure     differences, population-specific allelic action. \(^2\) inconsistency \(^2 = 100 \times \max(0,\, (Q - df)/Q)\).     Values > 50% indicate substantial -population heterogeneity. Block boundary concordance blocks_pop1     blocks_pop2 supplied, bp overlap ratio two     populations' block definitions computed block. ratio     < 0.8 flags blocks LD structure likely differs     populations effect comparisons interpreted cautiously. Addressing two principal limitations cross-population validation: Population structure confounding: Q+K mixed model     test_block_haplotypes() already corrects within-population     structure via haplotype GRM.  Cross-population validation     inherently controls -population confounding design:     haplotype allele must associate phenotype genetically     distinct background, making false-positive carry-Pop 's     stratification implausible.  meta-analytic \(^2\) statistic     additionally flags cases effect sizes heterogeneous     shared biological mechanism unlikely. LD block boundary differences: Block boundaries can differ     populations due different historical recombination rates     ancestral haplotype structure.  boundary_overlap_ratio     column quantifies directly every block.  Low overlap (< 0.8)     means two populations carve genomic region blocks     different sizes; case haplotype allele tested 50 kb     window Pop compared allele 30 kb window Pop B     strings match well.  n_shared_alleles     column empirical consequence: low shared-allele counts     despite adequate allele frequencies populations direct     symptom block boundary mismatch.  recommended remedy - passing     Pop 's block table blocks argument     test_block_haplotypes() Pop B - eliminates issue     entirely forcing runs use identical coordinates.

what: Cross-Population GWAS Effect Concordance from External Results — compare_gwas_effects
title: Cross-Population GWAS Effect Concordance from External Results — compare_gwas_effects
text: Compares haplotype block-level association signals two populations GWAS run externally (e.g. GAPIT, TASSEL, FarmCPU, PLINK, tool) rather test_block_haplotypes. function accepts external GWAS results two ways: Pre-mapped (recommended): supply output     define_qtl_regions population. QTL table     already maps marker LD block, providing lead SNP,     effect size (BETA), p-value per block.     reliable input block assignment explicit. Raw GWAS + blocks: supply raw GWAS data frames plus block     tables; function calls define_qtl_regions internally     map markers blocks comparing. compared : External GWAS produces marker-level effects, haplotype-allele-level effects. block level population contributes one observation: lead SNP (smallest p-value block). comparison therefore analogous two-sample Mendelian randomisation - one effect estimate per exposure (block) per population, combined via IVW meta-analysis. one "allele" per block (lead SNP), several statistics differ compare_block_effects: n_shared_alleles always 1 (lead SNP concept). effect_correlation always NA (needs >= 3 alleles). direction_agreement 0 1 (sign lead SNP effect agrees     ). Q_df always 0 (one observation per population; Cochran Q     undefined two populations one allele per block). meta_p tests whether IVW combined effect differs     zero - primary replication test. Standard error derivation: Many GWAS tools report BETA P SE. SE absent, compare_gwas_effects() derives z-score: $$SE = \frac{|\beta|}{|z|},\quad z = \Phi^{-1}(P/2)$$ \(\Phi^{-1}\) standard normal quantile function. exact large-sample Wald tests (dominant GWAS framework) provides valid SE IVW weighting. Interpreting pleiotropic blocks: trait_col supplied GWAS results contain multiple traits, function compares trait trait. Blocks significant multiple traits populations (pleiotropic = TRUE QTL tables) flagged both_pleiotropic = TRUE output, identifying robust cross-population replication targets.

title: Compare Haplotype Allele Frequencies Between Two Population Groups — compare_haplotype_populations
text: LD block, computes allele frequencies two sample groups returns FST (full multi-allelic Weir & Cockerham 1984 theta estimator, eq. 2-6: \(\theta = \sum_i a_i / \sum_i (a_i+b_i+c_i)\) across alleles \(\)), frequency differences, chi-squared test independence. Useful detecting blocks divergent selection monitoring diversity changes breeding cycles. phased haplotypes ("gamete1|gamete2" strings), true observed-heterozygosity component (\(c_i = \bar{h}_i/2\)) computed actual gamete pairs, matching original Weir & Cockerham (1984) diploid estimator exactly. unphased haplotype strings (per-individual diplotype calls, separable gametes – see extract_haplotypes), heterozygosity component observed set 0, reduces estimator valid "one gene copy per observation" special case rather approximating heterozygosity value recovered data.

title: Genomic Dominance Relationship Matrix (Vitezica et al. 2013) — compute_dominance_grm
text: SNP \(j\) reference-allele frequency \(p_j\) (dosage mean / 2) \(q_j = 1-p_j\), dominance incidence coding $$S_{ij} = \begin{cases} -2q_j^2 & \text{dose} = 0 \\ 2p_jq_j & \text{dose} = 1 \\ -2p_j^2 & \text{dose} = 2 \end{cases}$$ \(D = SS' / \sum_j (2p_jq_j)^2\). Dosage values rounded nearest genotype class (0/1/2) coding, warning value far integer call (e.g. imputed dosage probabilities rather hard genotype calls) – allele frequencies use original, unrounded dosage less biased estimate.

Whether haplotype feature matrix uses additive_012 encoding phased data (dosage values 0/1/2, dose scale = 2) unphased data (presence/absence 0/1, dose scale = 1). Instead samples pair indices SNP positions (genotype /O), collects unique SNP indices involved, calls read_chunk() compact set. 50,000 random pairs 500,000-SNP chromosome 500 individuals, peak RAM approximately 40 MB rather 2 GB. Use method = "r2" LD decay estimation; reserve method = "rV2" block detection. Sampling strategies: "sliding_window" Computes r\(^2\) within moving     window window_snps SNPs, reading columns per     step. Uses adaptive stride: window placed     approximately n_pairs / (window_snps*(window_snps-1)/2)     evenly-spaced positions across chromosome, total pairs     stays near n_pairs regardless marker density.     window_snps=50 500k-SNP chromosome     n_pairs=50000: stride=12,195, 41 read_chunk     calls instead 10,000. density guard automatically     switches chromosomes > 200,000 SNPs "random"     sampling (consecutive SNPs WGS density always near-     perfect LD, making sliding-window curve uninformative).     Matches TASSEL approach (Bradbury et al. 2007); recommended     chip-density panels (< 200k SNPs per chromosome). what: Compute Local Haplotype GEBV per Block (Tong et al. 2025) — compute_local_gebv
title: Compute Local Haplotype GEBV per Block (Tong et al. 2025) — compute_local_gebv
text: LD block, computes local GEBV (haplotype effect) every individual summing per-SNP additive effects alleles carry within block: $$\text{local GEBV}_f = \sum_{t \f} (x_t - 2 p_t)\,\alpha_t$$ \(x_t\) allele dosage (0/1/2) SNP \(t\), \(p_t\) SNP's population allele frequency, \(\alpha_t\) additive effect. Centering \(2p_t\) (rather heterozygote midpoint, dosage = 1) matches convention used backsolve_snp_effects derive alpha first place (\(\text{GEBV} = M\alpha\) \(M\) centred \(2p\)), summing local_gebv across every block one individual reconstructs individual's overall backsolved GEBV. Blocks ranked Var(local GEBV) – blocks high variance contribute strongly trait differences among individuals likely harbour causal loci (Tong et al. 2025). ranking unaffected choice centering point (variance shift-invariant), absolute local_gebv values meaningful – .e. summable back genome-wide GEBV – \(2p_t\) convention used .

what: When to use r^2 vs rV^2
title: Compute Standard r^2 LD Matrix — compute_r2
text: r^2 Use large unstructured datasets (> 500 k markers), random     mating populations, whenever speed matters. standard estimator     inflated related populations (.e. -estimate LD)     usually leads slightly conservative (larger) blocks rather     catastrophically wrong ones. rV^2 Use highly structured / related populations (livestock,     inbred lines, family-based human cohorts) kinship inflation     meaningfully distort block boundaries. Requires computing     inverting GRM - prohibitive beyond ~5 k individuals.

what: Estimate Diplotype Effects and Dominance Deviations Per LD Block — estimate_diplotype_effects
title: Estimate Diplotype Effects and Dominance Deviations Per LD Block — estimate_diplotype_effects
text: Fits per-block diplotype model decompose phenotypic variation additive dominance components LD block, correcting population structure kinship via haplotype GRM. function provides direct evidence non-additive gene action: dominance, overdominance, heterosis. Method: LD block, unique diplotypes (canonical haplotype-pair strings inferred infer_block_haplotypes, e.g. "010/110") treated levels fixed factor. mixed model haplotype GRM kinship random effect fitted via rrBLUP::mixed.solve() obtain de-regressed phenotype residuals. Diplotype class means computed residuals. pair common alleles (, B), classical quantitative genetics parameters derived three diplotype class means: Additive effect: \(= (\bar{y}_{BB} - \bar{y}_{AA}) / 2\) Dominance deviation: \(d = \bar{y}_{AB} -     (\bar{y}_{AA} + \bar{y}_{BB}) / 2\) Dominance ratio: \(d/\) - key quantity interpreting     gene action (see d_over_a column description).

title: Estimate Diplotype Effects and Dominance Deviations Per LD Block — estimate_diplotype_effects
text: haplotypes Named list produced extract_haplotypes. Phase-ambiguous diplotypes (unphased heterozygotes) excluded dominance analysis included omnibus F-test diplotype string unambiguous. accurate dominance decomposition, phased input (read_phased_vcf, phase_with_beagle, via phase_with_beagle) strongly recommended. blues Pre-adjusted phenotype means. Accepts four formats test_block_haplotypes: named numeric vector, single-trait data frame, multi-trait data frame, named list. formats require individual IDs matching names haplotype strings. blocks LD block table run_Big_LD_all_chr. Used supply block coordinate metadata (CHR, start_bp, end_bp) output tables. min_freq Numeric (0, 1). Minimum allele frequency. Alleles threshold full panel excluded dominance decomposition (dominance_table) diplotypes still contribute diplotype_means omnibus_tests sufficient individuals carry . Default 0.05. min_n_diplotype Integer. Minimum number individuals must carry given diplotype class included diplotype_means dominance decomposition. Diplotype classes fewer individuals silently excluded. omnibus F-test uses retained classes. Default 3L. Increasing 5-10 improves mean estimate stability small panels; decreasing 3 recommended. id_col Character. Name individual-ID column blues data frame. Default "id". blue_col Character. Name phenotype column single-trait data frames. Default "blue". blue_cols Character vector. Phenotype column names multi-trait data frames. Default NULL. sig_threshold Numeric (0, 1]. Significance cutoff applied p-value chosen sig_metric. Default 0.05. sig_metric Character. p-value drives significant flag $omnibus_tests. One : "p_omnibus_adj" (default) - plain Bonferroni:     \(\min(p \times n_{blocks},\,1)\), computed per trait.     Retained backward compatibility. "p_omnibus_fdr" - Benjamini-Hochberg FDR per trait. "p_omnibus_simplem" - simpleM Bonferroni-style:     \(\min(p \times M_{\mathrm{eff}},\,1)\),     \(M_{\mathrm{eff}}\) estimated eigenspectrum     block-summary PC1 matrix. "p_omnibus_simplem_sidak" - simpleM Sidak-style:     \(1-(1-p)^{M_{\mathrm{eff}}}\). Recommended: consistent     test_block_haplotypes. four p-value columns always present $omnibus_tests regardless choice. meff_percent_cut Numeric (0, 1). Proportion variance explained retained PCs simpleM eigendecomposition used estimate \(M_{\mathrm{eff}}\) sig_metric = "p_omnibus_simplem" "p_omnibus_simplem_sidak". Default 0.995 (99.5%), following original simpleM recommendation (Gao et al. 2008). meff_max_cols Integer. Maximum columns per eigendecomposition chunk estimating \(M_{\mathrm{eff}}\). Default 1000L. verbose Logical. TRUE (default) prints progress per trait.

title: Estimate Diplotype Effects and Dominance Deviations Per LD Block — estimate_diplotype_effects
text: named list class c("HapBlockR_diplotype", "list")   three elements: diplotype_means Data frame. One row per diplotype class per     LD block per trait, diplotype classes >= min_n_diplotype     individuals. Contains 9 columns: block_id (character) - Block identifier. CHR (character) - Chromosome. start_bp, end_bp (integer) - Block coordinates. trait (character) - Trait name. diplotype (character) - Canonical diplotype string: two         haplotype allele strings sorted alphabetically joined         "/", e.g. "010/110". Homozygotes identical         halves: "010/010". format ensures "010/110"         "110/010" always represented identically. n_class (integer) - Number individuals carrying         specific diplotype combination. n_total (integer) - Total individuals non-missing         data block (sum n_class across diplotype classes). mean_blue (numeric) - Mean de-regressed phenotype value         diplotype class (residual scale GRM correction). se_mean (numeric) - Standard error mean         (sd / sqrt(n_class)). dominance_table Data frame. One row per ordered allele pair     (, B) per block per trait, pairs three diplotype classes     (AA, AB, BB) >= min_n_diplotype individuals.     Contains 14 columns: block_id, CHR, start_bp, end_bp,         trait - . allele_A, allele_B (character) - two alleles         compared (alphabetically ordered: comes B). mean_AA, mean_AB, mean_BB (numeric) -         Diplotype class means de-regressed phenotype scale. (numeric) - Additive effect:         \((\bar{y}_{BB} - \bar{y}_{AA}) / 2\). Positive means allele B         increases trait value relative . d (numeric) - Dominance deviation:         \(\bar{y}_{AB} - (\bar{y}_{AA} + \bar{y}_{BB}) / 2\).         Positive: heterozygote advantage (overdominance \(|d| > ||\)).         Negative: heterozygote disadvantage (underdominance). d_over_a (numeric NA) - Dominance ratio         \(d/\). Interpretation: 0 = purely additive gene action;         \(\pm 0.5\) = partial dominance; \(\pm 1\) = complete dominance         (heterozygote equal one homozygote); \(|d/| > 1\) = overdominance         (heterozygote exceeds homozygotes - evidence heterosis         locus). NA \(|| < 10^{-10}\) (additive         variation homozygotes). overdominance (logical) - TRUE         \(|d/| > 1\) d_over_a NA. omnibus_tests Data frame. One row per LD block per trait,     blocks least min_n_diplotype individuals carry     least 2 distinct diplotype classes. Contains 9 columns: block_id, trait - . n_diplotypes (integer) - Number diplotype classes         >= min_n_diplotype individuals, used factor levels. F_stat (numeric) - F-statistic one-way ANOVA         (diplotype factor) de-regressed phenotype residuals. df1 (integer) - Numerator df = n_diplotypes - 1. df2 (integer) - Denominator df = n_obs - n_diplotypes. p_omnibus (numeric, (0,1]) - Raw p-value. p_omnibus_adj (numeric, (0,1]) - Bonferroni-adjusted         across tested blocks per trait. significant (logical) - TRUE         p_omnibus_adj < 0.05. Sorted ascending p_omnibus.

what: Estimate Per-SNP Marker Effects via GBLUP, rrBLUP (SNP-BLUP), or Bayesian Regression — estimate_marker_effects
title: Estimate Per-SNP Marker Effects via GBLUP, rrBLUP (SNP-BLUP), or Bayesian Regression — estimate_marker_effects
text: Unified "Step B" marker-effect estimator haplotype-stacking pipeline (see run_haplotype_prediction), mirroring flexibility HapSelect's create_marker_effects_file() offers (rrBLUP / BGLR / Sommer / ASReml-R – "model returns vector marker effects aligned map"). Returns named vector per-SNP additive effects centred-dosage (\(2p\)) scale used throughout HapBlockR, ready compute_local_gebv. "gblup" (default) Fits rrBLUP::kin.blup()     supplied genomic/haplotype relationship matrix G,     backsolves per-SNP effects resulting GEBV via     backsolve_snp_effects (VanRaden 2008; Tong et al. 2025),     using every individual present geno_matrix/G.     computation run_haplotype_prediction always     used internally, except function's bespoke "gblup" code path     restricts backsolving phenotyped subset backward     compatibility; calling estimate_marker_effects(method = "gblup")     directly backsolves full population instead. Requires     G. "rrblup" Fits rrBLUP::mixed.solve() directly     marker-effect (SNP-BLUP / ridge-regression BLUP) model,     \(y = \mu + Zu + e\) \(u \sim N(0, \sigma_u^2 )\)     (Meuwissen et al. 2001; Endelman 2011), returning u directly –     relationship matrix backsolving step needed. standard     equal-per-SNP-variance assumption mathematically equivalent     VanRaden GBLUP--backsolve, computed way around. "bayesb", "bayesc", "bayesa" Fit     BGLR::BGLR() corresponding variable-selection prior     (Perez & de los Campos 2014) directly genotype matrix, taking     posterior mean marker effects alpha. "bayesa"     BayesA (marker-specific variances scaled-inverse-chi-squared     prior, point mass zero); "bayesb"/"bayesc" add     point mass zero (variable selection). Note     "bayesr" option: BGLR implement four-component     mixture "BayesR" method (Erbe et al. 2012) – earlier version     function incorrectly assumed , fails runtime     BGLR::BGLR()'s "model BayesR implemented" error;     caught running test suite "bayesr" replaced     real BGLR model "bayesa". Requires BGLR     package (Suggests). BGLR runs MCMC sampler writes     temporary diagnostic files (removed automatically unless     bglr_dir supplied); markedly slower     "gblup"/"rrblup" , stochastic, exactly     reproducible seed set. four methods return gebv scale (\(\hat g = M \hat\alpha\), centred genotype matrix times estimated marker effects), results directly comparable across method choices – e.g. sanity-check one method's block ranking another's.

what: Fine-Map Epistatic SNP Pairs Within a Single Block — fine_map_epistasis_block
title: Fine-Map Epistatic SNP Pairs Within a Single Block — fine_map_epistasis_block
text: Exhaustively adaptively identifies specific SNP pairs within single LD block drive block-level epistatic signal. Three methods available: "pairwise" Exhaustive C(p,2) scan. Tests pairs using     model scan_block_epistasis. Recommended     blocks p <= 200 SNPs. "lasso" Fits LASSO model main effects     pairwise interaction terms using glmnet. Identifies     interaction terms non-zero coefficients cross-validated     lambda. Recommended blocks p > 200 SNPs. "auto" Dispatches "pairwise" p <= 200,     "lasso" otherwise.

text: Fast, scalable linkage disequilibrium (LD) block detection genome-wide SNP data using C++/Armadillo computational core two LD metrics: standard r^2 kinship-adjusted rV^2. title: HapBlockR: Genome-Wide LD Block Detection, Haplotype Analysis, Genomic Prediction, and Breeding Decision Support — HapBlockR-package

Suitable unstructured populations large datasets (10 M+ markers). rV^2 (method = "rV2") Kinship-whitened squared correlation     (Mangin et al. 2012, Heredity 108:285-291). Corrects LD inflation relatedness. livestock,     inbred lines, family-based cohorts < 200 k markers per chromosome.

title: HapBlockR: Genome-Wide LD Block Detection, Haplotype Analysis, Genomic Prediction, and Breeding Decision Support — HapBlockR-package
text: Read genotype data: read_geno – auto-detects CSV,     HapMap, VCF, GDS, BED, plain matrix. WGS panels peak RAM     concern, use read_geno_bigmemory build     memory-mapped store (requires bigmemory). Detect LD blocks chromosome-wise: run_Big_LD_all_chr. Optionally auto-tune parameters: tune_LD_params. Reconstruct haplotypes: extract_haplotypes. Decode haplotype strings nucleotides:     decode_haplotype_strings. Compute diversity metrics: compute_haplotype_diversity. Build prediction feature matrix:     build_haplotype_feature_matrix. Compute LD decay chromosome-specific decay distances:     compute_ld_decay. Provides critical r\(^2\)     threshold (parametric: 95th percentile unlinked-marker r\(^2\))     per-chromosome decay distances candidate gene windows. Map GWAS hits QTL regions (LD-aware windows     ld_decay supplied): define_qtl_regions. Genomic prediction (Tong et al. 2024/2025):     run_haplotype_prediction – full pipeline BLUEs     block importance; step--step via     compute_haplotype_grm,     backsolve_snp_effects,     compute_local_gebv,     rank_haplotype_blocks. Haplotype association testing simpleM correction     (Gao et al. 2008, 2010, 2011): test_block_haplotypes.     sig_metric selects among p_wald, p_fdr,     p_simplem (Bonferroni-style), p_simplem_sidak     (Sidak-style, recommended). four p-value columns always present.     meff_scope controls Meff estimation scope. Cross-population GWAS validation - two functions depending     association analysis performed: compare_block_effects - results         test_block_haplotypes. IVW meta-analysis, Cochran Q,         -squared, direction agreement per block. compare_gwas_effects - results external         GWAS tools (GAPIT, TASSEL, FarmCPU, PLINK, etc.). Accepts raw GWAS         data frames define_qtl_regions output. Derives SE         z-score absent. functions support block_match = "position" match         LD blocks genomic interval overlap (Intersection--Union) rather         block_id string equality. handles common case         block boundaries differ populations due different         ancestral LD structures. overlap_min (default 0.50) sets         minimum IoU valid positional match. match_type output         column reports "exact", "position",         "pop1_only" every block. Write outputs: write_haplotype_numeric,     write_haplotype_character,     write_haplotype_diversity. run everything : run_ldx_pipeline.

Cross-population effect concordance from external GWAS results. # Here ldx_gwas is used for both populations; in practice these # would be independent GWAS runs on separate cohorts. set.seed(1L) gwas_pop2        <- ldx_gwas gwas_pop2$BETA   <- ldx_gwas$BETA * 0.8 + rnorm(20, 0, 0.02) gwas_pop2$SE     <- ldx_gwas$SE   * 0.9 + runif(20, 0, 0.005) gwas_pop2$P      <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(gwas_pop2$BETA / gwas_pop2$SE))  # Path 1: pre-mapped (recommended for auditability) qtl1 <- define_qtl_regions(ldx_gwas,  ldx_blocks, ldx_snp_info,                            p_threshold = NULL, verbose = FALSE) qtl2 <- define_qtl_regions(gwas_pop2, ldx_blocks, ldx_snp_info,                            p_threshold = NULL, verbose = FALSE) conc <- compare_gwas_effects(   qtl_pop1    = qtl1,   qtl_pop2    = qtl2,   blocks_pop1 = ldx_blocks,   blocks_pop2 = ldx_blocks,   pop1_name   = "DiscoveryPop",   pop2_name   = "ReplicationPop",   verbose     = FALSE ) conc$concordance[, c("block_id","direction_agreement","meta_p","replicated")] #>                block_id direction_agreement       meta_p replicated #> 1    block_1_1000_25027                   1 1.855521e-10       TRUE #> 2   block_1_81064_99022                   1 1.687084e-11       TRUE #> 3 block_1_155368_179371                   1 3.037882e-14       TRUE #> 4    block_2_1000_30023                   1 1.409021e-07       TRUE #> 5  block_2_86236_105290                   1 3.304721e-07       TRUE #> 6    block_3_1000_19068                   1 7.263598e-03       TRUE  # Path 2: raw GWAS + blocks (calls define_qtl_regions internally) conc2 <- compare_gwas_effects(   gwas_pop1     = ldx_gwas,   gwas_pop2     = gwas_pop2,   blocks_pop1   = ldx_blocks,   blocks_pop2   = ldx_blocks,   snp_info_pop1 = ldx_snp_info,   p_threshold   = NULL,   verbose       = FALSE ) print(conc2) #> HapBlockR Cross-Population Effect Concordance #>   Populations: pop1 vs pop2 #>   Traits:       trait  #>   Blocks compared:           6  #>   With enough shared alleles: 6  #>   Directionally concordant:   6  #>   Replicated (dir + Q_p>0.05): 6  #>   Boundary warnings:          0 (overlap ratio < 0.8 ) #>   Shared allele comparisons:  6  # what: Prepare Genotype Matrix for LD Computation — prepare_geno
title: Prepare Genotype Matrix for LD Computation — prepare_geno
text: Central preparation function called inside Big_LD() run_Big_LD_all_chr. Depending method: "r2" Mean-centres SNP column. kinship needed.     Returns centred matrix directly. Fast - O(np). "rV2" Computes VanRaden GRM via AGHmatrix, tunes     via ASRgenomics, inverts via Cholesky/eigen, left-multiplies     centred genotype matrix. Returns whitened matrix     whitening factor use appendSGTs. Missing genotype calls     mean-imputed (0 already-centred scale) immediately     whitening: whitening step mixes individuals     together via n x n GRM-derived matrix, single unimputed     NA otherwise propagate across entire SNP column     every individual multiplied , just individual     missing call.

text: path Character. Path genotype file, R numeric matrix format = "matrix". format Character NULL. One "numeric", "hapmap", "vcf", "gds", "bed", "matrix". Default ",". clean_malformed Logical. title: Read Genotype Data into an HapBlockR Backend — read_geno
text: "numeric" CSV TXT, one row per SNP. Required columns:     SNP, CHR, POS, REF, ALT. Remaining     columns sample dosages {0, 1, 2, NA}. Extension: .csv,     .txt. "hapmap" Standard 11-column HapMap header followed sample     columns two-character nucleotide calls (AA, ,     NN missing). Extension: .hmp.txt. "vcf" VCF v4.2. phased (0|1) unphased     (0/1) GT fields accepted. Multi-allelic sites use first ALT.     Missing (./.) becomes NA. Extension: .vcf,     .vcf.gz. "gds" SNPRelate GDS file. Requires     BiocManager::install("SNPRelate"). Extension: .gds. "bed" PLINK binary BED. Companion .bim     .fam files must exist path stem. Extension:     .bed. "matrix" -memory R numeric matrix (individuals x SNPs,     0/1/2). Must supply snp_info separately.

text: geno_matrix Numeric matrix (individuals x SNPs; values 0/1/2), spanning chromosomes. snp_info Data frame columns CHR, SNP, POS. Column order flexible; columns matched name. CLQcut, clstgap, leng, subSegmSize, MAFcut, appendrare, close_gaps_with_snps, gap_k_rep, checkLargest, CLQmode, kin_method, split, digits, seed, verbose Forwarded Big_LD(). See function's documentation details. method Character. LD metric: "r2" (default, standard squared Pearson correlation) "rV2" (kinship-adjusted). See Big_LD() details. n_threads Integer. Number OpenMP threads C++ LD kernel. Default 1L. Increase multi-core systems. singleton_as_block Logical. TRUE, SNPs pass MAF filtering assigned clique returned single-SNP blocks (start == end, length_bp == 1). Default FALSE. See Big_LD() details. min_snps_chr Integer. Labels must match values snp_info$CHR normalisation (chr prefix). E.g. chr = c("1","3","5") chr = "X". Default NULL processes chromosomes. clean_malformed Logical. TRUE, stream-clean input file reading removing lines whose column count match header. relevant geno_matrix file path wrapped backend. Default FALSE. max_bp_distance Integer. Maximum base-pair distance SNP pair r\(^2\) computed. Pairs beyond distance set zero adjacency matrix (assumed negligible LD). 0L (default) disables computes pairs (original behaviour). Recommended value WGS panels: 500000L (500 kb). effect CLQmode "Louvain" "Leiden" window spans less max_bp_distance. Requires sorted SNP positions within sub-segment (guaranteed run_Big_LD_all_chr).

what: Haplotype Prediction and Block Importance from Pre-Adjusted Phenotypes — run_haplotype_prediction
title: Haplotype Prediction and Block Importance from Pre-Adjusted Phenotypes — run_haplotype_prediction
text: Runs complete Tong et al. (2025) haplotype stacking pipeline using pre-adjusted phenotype values (BLUEs, BLUPs, adjusted entry means). Accepts either single trait multiple traits simultaneously. single trait supplied, GBLUP fitted via rrBLUP::kin.blup() block importance ranked Var(local GEBV) trait. multiple traits supplied, single trait-agnostic GRM computed shared across traits. rrBLUP::kin.blup() fitted per trait using shared GRM. Block importance summarised across traits per-trait columns plus cross-trait aggregates.

text: geno_matrix Numeric matrix (individuals x SNPs), values 0/1/2/NA. Row names must genotype IDs. snp_info Data frame columns SNP, CHR, POS. blocks Block table run_Big_LD_all_chr. blues Pre-adjusted phenotype values. See section accepted formats. id_col Name ID column blues data frame. Default "id". blue_col Name BLUE column single-trait data frames. Default "blue". blue_cols Character vector trait column names multi-trait data frames. Default NULL – numeric non-ID columns used. importance_rule set combined important flag multi-trait results: "" (default): TRUE important >= 1 trait. "": TRUE important traits. "mean": TRUE var_scaled_mean >= 0.9. Ignored single-trait runs (single-trait important always scaled variance >= 0.9). top_n Integer NULL. Max haplotype alleles per block. Default NULL. min_freq Minimum haplotype allele frequency. Default 0.01. min_snps Minimum SNPs per block. Default 3L. affects haplotype feature matrix used GRM/diversity (hap_matrix, haplotypes); local GEBV decomposition governed separately complete_decomposition. bend Logical. Add ridge GRM diagonal. Default TRUE. marker_effect_method One "gblup" (default), "rrblup", "bayesb", "bayesc", "bayesa". See Marker-effect estimation methods section. include_dominance Logical, default FALSE. Fit joint additive + dominance model instead additive-. valid marker_effect_method = "gblup"; requires BGLR. See Additive + dominance GBLUP section. complete_decomposition Logical. Default TRUE. Passed compute_local_gebv: guarantees every SNP known effect attributed block (singleton pseudo-block covered blocks), rowSums(local_gebv) reconstructs individual's full backsolved GEBV – matching HapSelect's completeness guarantee localGEBV. Set FALSE restore previous behaviour (SNPs outside every block window dropped). importance_threshold Numeric (0,1]. Scaled-variance cutoff important flag (single-trait, multi-trait importance_rule = "mean"). Default 0.9 (unchanged previous releases). See also select_top_blocks count/percentage/cumulative-variance selection instead fixed cutoff. n_iter, burn_in Integer. MCMC iterations / burn-, used marker_effect_method "bayesb"/"bayesc"/"bayesa". Defaults 6000/1000. seed Integer NULL. Random seed Bayesian methods (ignored otherwise). Default NULL. verbose Logical. Print progress. Default TRUE. ploidy Integer >= 2. Ploidy level geno_matrix's dosage encoding. Default 2L (diploid, unchanged previous releases). Passed backsolve_snp_effects/ estimate_marker_effects/compute_local_gebv marker effects local GEBVs use ploidy-generalised VanRaden centering (\(\text{ploidy} \cdot p\) instead \(2p\)). affect shared GRM (G), always built haplotype-allele feature matrix – derived HapBlockR's diploid-hap1/hap2 phased representation, dosage columns always 0/1/2 regardless argument. Set geno_matrix holds raw 0..ploidy dosage calls higher-ploidy species.
