title: Haplotype Prediction and Block Importance from Pre-Adjusted Phenotypes — run_haplotype_prediction
text: traits fitted using rrBLUP::kin.blup() per-trait loop sharing GRM. produces numerically identical results sommer::mmes() single-trait models (verified empirically 4 decimal places), avoiding multi-trait cbind() formula fails sommer <= 4.4.5 (Armadillo fixed-size matrix error C++ coefficient matrix construction). traits use GRM, cross-trait block importance values directly comparable. solver_used "rrBLUP" default marker_effect_method = "gblup"; see next section methods.

title: Haplotype Prediction and Block Importance from Pre-Adjusted Phenotypes — run_haplotype_prediction
text: marker_effect_method selects "Step B" pipeline – per-SNP effects derived summing within block (Step C). four options ultimately call estimate_marker_effects produce snp_effects vector centred-dosage scale, local_gebv/block_importance comparable across methods: "gblup" (default) rrBLUP::kin.blup()     haplotype-block GRM, backsolved per-SNP effects     (backsolve_snp_effects; VanRaden 2008; Tong et al. 2025).     method pipeline always used. "rrblup" rrBLUP::mixed.solve() fit directly     marker-effect (SNP-BLUP / ridge-regression) model – relationship     matrix backsolving step (Meuwissen et al. 2001; Endelman 2011). "bayesb", "bayesc", "bayesa" Bayesian     variable-selection regression via BGLR::BGLR() (Perez & de los     Campos 2014). Requires BGLR package. Slower (MCMC)     stochastic unless seed set. ("bayesr" option –     BGLR implement four-component-mixture "BayesR" method;     see estimate_marker_effects's documentation.) Mirrors flexibility HapSelect's create_marker_effects_file() (rrBLUP / BGLR / Sommer / ASReml-R).

title: Haplotype Prediction and Block Importance from Pre-Adjusted Phenotypes — run_haplotype_prediction
text: default (include_dominance = FALSE), pipeline – like estimate_marker_effects – additive-. Set include_dominance = TRUE (marker_effect_method = "gblup") fit joint additive + dominance model instead: compute_dominance_grm builds dominance relationship matrix \(G_D\) (Vitezica, Varona & Legarra 2013) raw SNP dosage matrix, paired existing haplotype-block additive GRM \(G_A\) two random-effect kernels single BGLR::BGLR(ETA = list(list(K = G_A, model = "RKHS"), list(K = G_D, model = "RKHS"))) call – rrBLUP::kin.blup() (default GBLUP solver) accepts single relationship matrix partition additive/dominance variance. Relevant trait suspected heterosis/overdominance, estimate_diplotype_effects can already flag per block via d/ratio. Requires BGLR package. Adds dominance_deviation, total_genetic_value (gebv + dominance_deviation), G_dominance return value (NULL include_dominance = FALSE, return list's field names stable regardless argument). Scope limit: per-SNP/per-block decomposition (snp_effects, local_gebv, block_importance) remains additive-even include_dominance = TRUE – backsolve_snp_effects additive-formula, block-level dominance decomposition settled methodology (see compute_dominance_grm's documentation).

title: Finlay-Wilkinson Stability Analysis of Haplotype Effects Across Environments — run_haplotype_stability
text: Estimates stability haplotype block's effect across multiple environments using Finlay-Wilkinson (1963) regression. block, per-environment GEBV contribution regressed environment mean (environmental index). regression slope b_i = 1 indicates average stability; b_i > 1 = -average response (exploits good environments); b_i < 1 = -average response (robust across environments).

title: Between-Block Haplotype Allele Epistasis Scan — scan_block_by_block_epistasis
text: Tests interactions haplotype allele dosage columns different LD blocks. significant allele (test_block_haplotypes), tests interaction every haplotype allele blocks: $$y = \mu + \alpha_i x_i + \alpha_j x_j + \gamma_{ij}(x_i x_j) + \varepsilon$$ Restricting significant alleles x blocks gives O(n_sig x n_total_alleles) tests – tractable WGS scale. panel: ~25 significant alleles x 17,943 alleles = ~450,000 tests. trans-haplotype epistasis scan: tests whether effect resistance haplotype one block depends haplotype background another block – form genetic background dependence single-SNP even single-block analyses detect.

what: Within-Block Pairwise SNP Epistasis Scan — scan_block_epistasis
title: Within-Block Pairwise SNP Epistasis Scan — scan_block_epistasis
text: Tests pairwise SNP x SNP interactions within haplotype blocks identified significant test_block_haplotypes. significant block, C(p, 2) SNP pairs tested interaction using model: $$y = \mu + a_i x_i + a_j x_j + aa_{ij}(x_i x_j) + \varepsilon$$ GRM-corrected REML residuals (null model test_block_haplotypes), ensuring tests population-structure-corrected. Restricting significant blocks avoids genome-wide explosion pairwise tests: 15 significant blocks ~200 SNPs , total number tests ~300,000, compared ~4.4 billion unrestricted genome-wide scan.

title: Score Individual Haplotype Portfolios Against Known Allele Effects — score_favorable_haplotypes
text: Scores individual's genome-wide haplotype composition table per-allele effects (genomic prediction association analysis), producing per-block score genome-wide stacking index. primary tool translating haplotype genomic prediction results actionable breeding rankings. Scoring rule: individual \(\) LD block \(b\), block score : $$s_{ib} = \sum_{j} \hat{\alpha}_j \cdot d_{ij}$$ \(\hat{\alpha}_j\) known effect allele \(j\) \(d_{ij}\) dosage (copies) allele \(j\) carried individual \(\) (0/1 unphased data; 0/1/2 phased data). genome-wide stacking index sum block scores across scored blocks, optionally normalised [0, 1].

title: Core-Collection / Diversity-Maximizing Subset Selection — select_core_collection
text: "maximin" (Default.) Farthest-point traversal (Gonzalez     1985): start single genetically distant pair,     repeatedly add whichever remaining candidate largest MINIMUM     distance everything already selected. Maximizes smallest     pairwise distance final set (guards near-duplicate     individuals slipping ), proven 2-approximation guarantee.     standard "M strategy" core-collection literature. "mean_distance" step, adds whichever remaining     candidate increases selected set's MEAN pairwise distance     ("MD strategy"). Tends spread selection evenly across     whole diversity space rather prioritising single     extreme outliers; expensive compute (recomputed per candidate     per step) still tractable typical core-collection sizes. Neither exact solver objective (standard greedy heuristics used throughout core-collection literature, guaranteed-optimal search) – see validate_crosses_exact need true optimum small-enough problem (function targets cross selection specifically, subset-diversity problem, shares "exact validation heuristic" philosophy).

title: Block-Level Haplotype Association Testing (Q+K Mixed Linear Model with simpleM Multiple-Testing Correction) — test_block_haplotypes
text: Performs genome-wide haplotype block association tests one quantitative traits. LD block tested unit: per-allele Wald tests identify specific haplotype alleles drive association, omnibus F-test evaluates block whole. Population structure kinship corrected jointly unified mixed linear model. addition raw FDR-adjusted p-values, function applies simpleM-style multiple-testing correction account correlation among tested haplotype alleles. simpleM estimates effective number independent tests (\(M_{\mathrm{eff}}\)) eigenvalues haplotype allele correlation matrix derives either Bonferroni-style Sidak-style adjusted threshold. Statistical model (Q+K / EMMAX formulation): $$y = \mu + \alpha \cdot x_{\mathrm{hap}} +        \sum_{k=1}^{K} \beta_k \, PC_k + g + \varepsilon$$ \(x_{\mathrm{hap}}\) Haplotype allele dosage (0, 1, 2 copies     phased data; 0 1 unphased). \(PC_k\) k-th eigenvector haplotype GRM,     fixed-effect covariate population structure. \(g \sim MVN(0,\,\sigma_g^2 G)\) Polygenic background     random effect. \(\varepsilon \sim MVN(0,\,\sigma_e^2 )\) Residual error. null model (\(\sigma_g^2\), \(\sigma_e^2\)) fit per trait via rrBLUP::mixed.solve() (REML). marker tested true GLS/EMMAX transform: phenotype every haplotype-allele column pre-multiplied \(\hat V^{-1/2}\), \(\hat V = \hat\sigma_g^2 G + \hat\sigma_e^2 \), via null model's GRM eigendecomposition (computed per trait reused every marker), transformed null design (intercept + PCs) projected via Frisch-Waugh-Lovell theorem per-allele per-block tests. mathematically equivalent full per-marker GLS fit \(\hat V\), approximation. null-model fit, GRM eigendecomposition, transformed null-design inversion fails, function falls back faster residual-scan approximation (subtracting estimated fixed effects polygenic BLUP, OLS remains) emits warning identifying affected trait. simpleM extension (Gao et al. 2008, 2010, 2011): \(M_{\mathrm{eff}}\) estimated eigenspectrum haplotype allele dosage correlation matrix - number principal components needed explain meff_percent_cut variance (default 99.5%). Two simpleM adjusted p-value paths always computed: p_simplem - Bonferroni-style:     \(\min(p \times M_{\mathrm{eff}},\,1)\). p_simplem_sidak - Sidak-style:     \(1 - (1 - p)^{M_{\mathrm{eff}}}\). haplotype alleles correlated within across nearby blocks, simpleM less conservative raw Bonferroni still providing family-wise error control.

title: Usefulness Criterion (UC) / Genomic Mating: Rank Candidate Crosses — usefulness_criterion
text: classical UC formula assumes infinite, normally-distributed progeny population. Real biparental crosses produce tens hundred progeny, TRUE expected selection intensity finite sample somewhat smaller asymptotic formula gives (order-statistics theory: expected mean top k n draws converges , equal, top-p-quantile density ratio n grows). Supplying n_progeny switches Monte Carlo estimate exact finite-sample intensity (see n_sim, seed) rather approximate closed-form small-sample correction – deliberately, since several closed-form corrections exist literature mutually consistent, whereas finite-sample order-statistic mean estimable directly exactly (Monte Carlo error) simulation. Leave n_progeny = NULL use standard asymptotic formula (fine large planned progeny numbers, pre-existing default behaviour). variance modes, predicted_variance reflects segregation target blocks block_importance , whole genome – tractability trade-select_parents_ga makes pre-filtering manageable set top-ranked blocks. block_importance covers blocks explaining local-GEBV variance (e.g. via select_top_blocks), captures segregating variance matters practice, exactly whole-genome quantity classical UC formulations assume. mid_parent_gebv (mean term), contrast, always uses full whole-genome gebv supply, since best available estimate cross's mean.

title: HapBlockR 0.3.12.9000 (development)
text: select_parents_by_family()’s family-quota shortlist strategy gains seven related improvements, addressed together one coherent rework rather piecemeal: BREAKING: family ranking shrinkage-corrected default. family’s raw top-rank_k mean score unreliable estimator true quality family small — classical small-sample noise quantitative genetics normally corrects via shrinkage/BLUP-style family evaluation rather trusting raw sample mean regardless many observations ’s built . new default, family_rank_method = "shrunk_topk_mean", estimates -family within-family/residual variance components every eligible member’s raw score via standard one-way random-effects ANOVA method--moments estimator (Searle, Casella & McCulloch 1992), shrinks family’s topk_mean toward across-family mean resulting empirical-Bayes/BLUP reliability weight w_f = n_f*tau2 /   (n_f*tau2 + sigma2) (Robinson 1991) — family 1 pulled hard toward pack; large family’s genuine top-k average trusted almost fully. can change family rank order relative previous releases whenever chosen families differ meaningfully size. Relatedness control (within_group_target_degree, G). Whenever relationship matrix G supplied, realised mean pairwise relationship final shortlist — overall ($mean_relationship) per selected family/group (family_ranking$mean_relationship) — now always reported, mirroring select_parents_ga()’s diagnostic, present regardless whether anything asked optimise . top , new within_group_target_degree argument ([0, 90], convention select_parents_ga()/select_parents_ocs() use) turns actual dial: filling family’s quota stops pure score-order truncation instead balances score relatedness ceiling, interpolated family’s top-scoring feasible subset select_core_collection(strategy = "maximin") restricted members (proven 2-approximation, Gonzalez 1985). Existing calls rely haplotypes’ allele-level dominant-block collision resolution now pass diversity_method = "dominant_block" explicitly, since haplotypes ignored new default. Uneven per-family/per-group quotas. n_per_family may now single integer (flat quota, unchanged default) named integer vector (explicit override per chosen family/group). Optional genetic-cluster grouping (group_by, n_clusters, cluster_method). group_by = "genetic_cluster" (alongside default, group_by = "family") builds groups directly G via hierarchical clustering (Ward’s minimum-variance linkage, cluster_method = "ward.D2" default) distance matrix implied G (identity select_core_collection() uses), cut n_clusters groups — programmes pedigree labels aren’t fully faithful proxy actual relatedness. pedigree family label genetic-cluster label reported per selected individual whenever available (by_family$family / by_family$genetic_group), independent one actually drove selection decision ($group_by echoes ), caller using genetic clusters quota logic can still see pick’s pedigree family cross-referencing, vice versa. what: Changed: usefulness_criterion(variance_model = "simplemating") no longer errors on heterozygous genotypes by default
title: HapBlockR 0.3.12.9000 (development)
text: Previously, heterozygous (dosage = 1) call anywhere geno_matrix made mode error immediately (SimpleMating::getUsefA() requires strictly 0/2/NA, fully homozygous DH/RIL-style calls). Real breeding programmes’ genotypes usually supplied ordinary 0/1/2 dosage realistically carry least residual heterozygosity even advanced inbred material, made mode impractical use without manually pre-processing geno_matrix first. Added het_to_na (default TRUE): heterozygous calls now automatically treated missing (set NA) calling SimpleMating::getUsefA(), usefulness_criterion() proceeds normally. defensible statistical choice, fabricated one — heterozygous cell marked “confident homozygous call ”, never rounded 0 2 (invent specific allele call data support), NA already valid value argument even het_to_na existed (SimpleMating::getUsefA() already receives handles missing calls normal way). verbose = TRUE, message reports exactly many calls (count %) converted. Values outside 0/1/2/NA still error unconditionally, since ’s defensible automatic interpretation . Set het_to_na = FALSE restore previous strict behaviour. tests/testthat/test-genomic-mating.R updated: old “errors loudly heterozygous” test now verifies new default succeeds (expected message), plus new test confirms het_to_na = FALSE still errors, new test confirms genuinely invalid dosage values (e.g. 9) still error regardless. scripts/CIAT_Peru_parent_selection.R’s stage 13b updated list het_to_na = TRUE explicitly reflect heterozygosity longer likely cause cross-check’s tryCatch() safety net ever fires.

what: Added: usefulness_criterion(variance_model = "linked") now accepts ld_matrix as an alternative to genetic_map
title: HapBlockR 0.3.12.9000 (development)
text: Previously “linked” unconditionally required real genetic map (genetic_map: SNP, CHR, cM), fallback — unlike “simplemating”, already accepted ld_matrix (SNP x SNP LD, used 1 - LD recombination- fraction proxy) map available. Added fallback “linked”: genetic_map NULL, target blocks instead ordered physical position (CHR, start_bp; new internal .block_physical_positions()) recombination fraction pair adjacent blocks proxied 0.5 * (1 - mean(LD)) (mean pairwise SNP r-squared two blocks’ member SNPs; new internal .adjacent_r_from_ld()) — [0, 0.5] range boundary behaviour Haldane’s mapping function, hand- verified exact closed-form values (LD = 1 -> r = 0; LD = 0 -> r = 0.5; known intermediate LD value) tests/testthat/test-genomic-mating.R section 6c, plus end--end usefulness_criterion() tests mirroring existing genetic_map-based ones. Important caveat, documented roxygen NEWS visibility: monotonic PROXY, validated genetic-distance estimator — LD reflects population-level historical recombination, drift, selection, necessarily true recombination fraction specific cross. Prefer genetic_map one; fall back ld_matrix don’t. Also, ld_matrix relaxes genetic-map requirement — “linked” (like “phased”) still unconditionally requires phased haplotypes either way, since population-level LD substitute knowing alleles specific individual’s two chromosomes actually carry.

what: New: variance_model = "linked" in usefulness_criterion() — native, linkage-aware progeny variance
title: HapBlockR 0.3.12.9000 (development)
text: Closes “UC’s variance model block-independent, linkage blocks” gap without adding GitHub-SimpleMating dependency existing variance_model = "simplemating" option requires. Given phased-haplotype/snp_info/snp_effects input "phased", plus genetic_map (SNP/CHR/cM), "linked" simulates n_sim_linked (default 2000L) Monte Carlo progeny: parent’s transmitted gamete generated block--block crossover walk along genetic map, recombination fraction adjacent target blocks Haldane’s (1919) mapping function (independent assortment, r = 0.5, across chromosome boundaries). closes “phased” mode’s “target blocks summed independently” simplification — blocks close together genetic map now correlated way real linkage requires. Implemented first-principles Monte Carlo (Haldane’s mapping function + standard Markov-chain crossover walk) rather hand-derived closed-form multi-locus covariance formula, deliberately mirroring package’s existing risk-avoidance precedent .run_simplemating_uc(). Hand- verified test-genomic-mating.R two exact closed-form boundary cases: blocks placed far enough apart r -> 0.5 (must recover independent sum "phased"’s per-block variance) blocks r = 0 (must recover exact 4-combo enumeration treating whole multi-block region one fused super-locus), plus monotonicity check intermediate r, RNG-non-disturbance check, end--end usefulness_criterion() smoke/validation tests. scope "phased": single-cross F1-style segregation variance, multi-generation RIL/DH population variance (remains "simplemating"’s type/generation territory).

what: Fixed: 8 failures surfaced by the first real devtools::test() run of this cycle
title: HapBlockR 0.3.12.9000 (development)
text: first devtools::test() run development cycle real R installation found genuine bugs alongside test-authoring mistakes: make_phased() test fixture (tests/testthat/helper.R) missing dosage/sample_ids. extract_haplotypes()’s phased-list branch requires full read_phased_vcf()-shaped list (hap1/hap2/dosage/sample_ids), just hap1/hap2 — omitting dosage sent NULL-dosage code path failed argument length zero. broke test-genomic-mating.R test-extensions.R fixture-construction time, meaning every test test-genomic-mating.R never actually executed (syntax-checked) run. Fixed making make_phased() return shape read_phased_vcf() produces. test-core-collection.R two calls select_core_collection() passing distance matrix (.cc_D, diagonal = 0) without type =   "distance", default type = "relationship" misinterpreted Gram matrix derived -zero pairwise distances. Fixed adding explicit type = "distance" argument. test-parent-selection.R compared sort(res$selected) numerically-ordered expected vector (paste0("ind", 6:10)), R’s default string sort lexicographic ("ind10" sorts "ind6"). Fixed switching expect_setequal(), since selection order doesn’t matter assertions. test-association.R’s zscore-formula test recomputed mean/sd score_favorable_haplotypes()’s already-rounded (normalize = FALSE) output rounded , compounding two roundings function’s single internal rounding — ~1e-6 mismatch, formula error. Fixed loosening comparison tolerance. test-genomic-mating.R’s .selection_intensity() “keeping ~everyone” test used p = 0.9, n_progeny = 5L, assuming round(0.9 * 5) = round(4.5) rounds 5 (triggering function’s k >= n_progeny early return). R’s round() uses round-half--even (“banker’s rounding”), round(4.5) = 4, 5 — test hitting ordinary Monte Carlo path (selecting top 4 5) correctly getting nonzero intensity (~0.29), bug .selection_intensity() . test also never executed run (fixture-construction failure ). Fixed using p = 0.99, n_progeny = 10L (round(9.9) = 10 unambiguously, .5-tie rounding involved) reliably exercise intended branch.

what: New: strategies 4-6 — Pareto selection, exact ILP validation, core collections
title: HapBlockR 0.3.12.9000 (development)
text: Completes six-strategy parent-selection roadmap (1: coancestry-penalised GA; 2: usefulness_criterion(); 3: select_parents_ocs(); 4-6: entry). pareto_front() (new file R/pareto_selection.R) — general, dependency-free non-dominated-sort utility (standard  pairwise-dominance algorithm plus NSGA-II crowding distance secondary diagnostic). Works data frame objective columns, e.g. usefulness_criterion() output. select_parents_pareto() (file) — sweeps select_parents_ga()’s coancestry_weight across grid Pareto-filters resulting (merit, relatedness) points empirical frontier, can see actual gain-vs-diversity tradeoff curve instead guessing single coancestry_weight value. Built entirely top already-implemented, already-verified GA solver – new optimisation algorithm (e.g. NSGA-II) hand-built . validate_crosses_exact() (new file R/exact_validation.R) — genuine EXACT solver (binary integer linear programming via lpSolve package) core cross-selection problem every tool package approximates heuristically (SimpleMating’s selectCrosses()/GOCS(), AlphaMate, GA). Deliberately scoped small-scale validation/sanity-check tool (max_vars safety cap), production workflow replacement. Deliberately support per-parent minimum-contribution hard constraint (SimpleMating’s min.cross) — exactly enforcing “min_cross applies parents used ” requires conditional big-M formulation, well-known source subtle ILP bugs, function’s entire purpose trustworthy reference; max_cross (simple unconditional upper bound) total n_cross count implemented straightforward linear constraints instead. New guarded lpSolve Suggests: dependency. select_core_collection() (new file R/core_collection.R) — classical core-collection / diversity-maximising subset problem (Schoen & Brown 1993), earlier strategies treat diversity constraint top merit objective, treats diversity objective (optional merit floor via .apply_merit_floor() used truncation_selection()/select_parents_ga()). Implemented standard farthest-point/maximin greedy heuristic (Gonzalez 1985, proven 2-approximation) mean-distance (“MD strategy”) alternative — simple, exactly-verifiable greedy algorithms, external dependency, execution-testing risk (unlike package’s statistical-model-heavy functions). Converts relationship matrix genetic distance via exact identity , approximation. four new exports (pareto_front, select_parents_pareto, validate_crosses_exact, select_core_collection) balance-verified; man/*.Rd still needed via devtools::document(), every function added development cycle.

text: Two related additions reviewing current (2025) source Resende-Lab/SimpleMating (Peixoto et al. 2024) directly, rather relying paper’s description older 2021 prototype package author hand: usefulness_criterion() gains variance_model = "simplemating", wrapping SimpleMating::getUsefA(). rigorous three variance modes now available: builds genuine multi-locus Mendelian-sampling covariance matrix per chromosome genetic-map recombination fractions (Haldane-mapped) LD-matrix proxy, following Lehermeier et al. (2017) – linkage across every supplied SNP, just within/across independently-summed LD blocks like existing "block_independent"/ "phased" modes. Real constraint, worked around: requires geno_matrix coded strictly 0/2 (fully homozygous DH/RIL-style calls) – appropriate heterozygous outbred parents, two native modes remain right choice. New arguments: geno_matrix, G, genetic_map/ld_matrix, type, generation, n_threads. select_parents_ocs()’s engine = "optisel" now wraps SimpleMating::GOCS() instead calling optiSel::candes()/opticont() directly. original direct-optiSel implementation written without working R interpreter available , comparison GOCS()’s actual verified source, turned real argument-name mismatches (guessed kinship=/ub.kinship=/ub.n=/method="max.bv"; GOCS()’s working code uses sKin=/flat ub=/method="max.Crit"). Rather patch guesses, engine now wraps GOCS() directly, tested implementation. One consequence: GOCS() shares AlphaMate’s Kinghorn-frontier-degree concept, ub_mean_kinship gone — target_degree now single diversity-vs- gain lever engines (numerically identical , just conceptually dial). Two real, now-verified GOCS() limitations surfaced honestly rather hidden: fixes parent’s contribution cap internally 2/n_candidates (max_contrib_per_parent/ n_parents_max configurable engine, unlike "alphamate"), mating allocator guarantee -repeated-matings allocation way AlphaMate’s evolutionary algorithm (checked afterward via $ok instead). package’s .allocate_matings_from_contributions() native allocator, longer used, removed. New SimpleMating guarded Suggests: dependency (Remotes: github::Resende-Lab/SimpleMating, CRAN), used features . optiSel remains separate Suggests: entry since select_parents_ocs()’s optiSel engine still requires directly (dependency SimpleMating::GOCS()). Original entry select_parents_ocs(), superseded left context: originally shipped hand-written optiSel::candes()/opticont() call native mate-allocator, turned need fixing GOCS()’s real source available. covered either OCS engine: family/cross--origin representation hard constraint (relevant population-improvement programme wants every family represented cycle) — family accepted output labelling .

title: HapBlockR 0.3.12.9000 (development)
text: Full audit every formula package used inform breeding decision (GEBV/GBLUP, GRM, selection index, parent selection, UC/genomic mating, forward simulation, marker effects, diversity/coancestry metrics), current best-established methods. held well -(VanRaden GRM, GBLUP/RR-BLUP/BayesA/B/C marker-effect dispatcher, Falconer /d diplotype decomposition, Weir & Cockerham FST). Three gaps addressed cycle (fourth, Smith-Hazel multi-trait selection index, explicitly scoped — user already strong external ASReml-based pipeline ): New compute_dominance_grm() (R/haplotypes.R) — genomic dominance relationship matrix D via Vitezica, Varona & Legarra (2013) natural--orthogonal parametrisation, diploid/biallelic , computed raw SNP genotype matrix (multi-allelic haplotype-block feature matrix, dominance formula isn’t well established). package fit dual-kernel (G_A + G_D) model — D meant paired compute_haplotype_grm()’s G fit externally (e.g. sommer::mmer(), ASReml), external-handoff pattern prepare_gblup_inputs() already uses G alone. new dependency. Finite-population selection intensity usefulness_criterion() – new n_progeny, n_sim, seed arguments. classical UC formula’s selection intensity assumes infinite progeny population, overstates i_sel realistic biparental cross sizes (tens hundred progeny). Supplying n_progeny switches .selection_intensity() Monte Carlo estimate true finite-sample expected order-statistic mean, rather one several mutually-inconsistent closed-form small-sample corrections literature — exact Monte Carlo error, doesn’t require trusting -memory constant. Default behaviour (n_progeny = NULL) unchanged. normalize_method score_favorable_haplotypes() — new "zscore" option alongside existing "minmax" (still default, backward compatibility). Min-max [0,1] rescaling direct genetic interpretation sensitive panel’s single extreme individual; z-score standardisation (genetic SD units) standard quantitative-genetics convention robust panel composition changes. Deliberately deferred, done cycle (substantial enough warrant review pass): linkage-aware (-block) variance mode usefulness_criterion() — scientifically strongest version use Monte Carlo gamete simulation via already-integrated genomicSimulation package rather hand-derived closed-form multi-locus covariance formula, since latter hard verify without able execute R environment; extending ga_vs_ts_simulation()’s forward-simulation comparison include UC-informed (, built, OCS-informed) recurrent-selection strategy alongside truncation selection, evaluating diversity-vs-gain tradeoffs multiple cycles.

what: New: usefulness_criterion() — rank candidate crosses (genomic mating)
title: HapBlockR 0.3.12.9000 (development)
text: Second six planned parent-selection strategy extensions. New file R/genomic_mating.R, new exported function usefulness_criterion(). truncation_selection() select_parents_ga() choose set parents, usefulness_criterion() instead ranks pairs candidate parents (crosses) classic Usefulness Criterion (Schnell & Utz 1975; Bernardo 2003; Zhong & Jannink 2007): UC = mid-parent GEBV + selection_intensity * sqrt(predicted cross variance) can surface crosses strong transgressive-segregation potential whole-genome GEBV ranking alone miss (genuinely good already-similar pair parents scores lower complementary pair predicted segregate wider progeny distribution). Two variance-prediction modes, selected user via variance_model (implemented; package choose one — pick whichever matches genotype data ): "block_independent" (default) — unphased-compatible, uses local_gebv (per-individual, per-block local GEBV) standard single-locus biparental segregation-variance formula per block, summed across target blocks. New segregation_factor argument (default 0.5) exposes formula’s scaling constant rather hard-coding . "phased" — requires phased haplotypes. Reads parent’s two actual haplotype alleles per block via infer_block_haplotypes(), computes per-allele effects new, strictly-validated internal helper (deliberately reusing decompose_block_effects(), found work silently drop every block given phased input – see “Known issue” note ), exactly enumerates 4 equally-likely gamete-pair combinations per block exact within-block segregation mean/variance. modes, predicted_variance covers blocks block_importance argument supply (tractability trade-select_parents_ga() already makes) — documented explicitly ?usefulness_criterion isn’t mistaken whole-genome quantity. mean term (mid_parent_gebv) always uses full whole-genome gebv supply. Scope, also documented ?usefulness_criterion: ranks candidate crosses, select parent set , allocate differential progeny numbers constrain population-wide inbreeding way true Optimal Contribution Selection (OCS, strategy 3 6, yet implemented) . new package dependencies — uses stats (qnorm, dnorm, var) utils (combn), already Imports. Known issue found building feature (now fixed — see “Fixed: decompose_block_effects()…” entry top file): decompose_block_effects() silently returned effects block given phased (“h1|h2”-style) haplotype input — digit-parsing logic assumed unphased fixed-width dosage strings, length check never matched block dropped warning. usefulness_criterion()’s phased mode avoided entirely helper time note written; decompose_block_effects() since fixed directly now safe use phased haplotypes. Still needed: man/usefulness_criterion.Rd (run devtools::document()), functions added cycle.

what: Merit-floor filtering and GA replication rigour for parent selection
title: HapBlockR 0.3.12.9000 (development)
text: truncation_selection() select_parents_ga() gain shared eligibility floor, select_parents_ga() gains built-replication/convergence diagnostics — closing gaps surfaced comparing HapBlockR’s parent selection real breeding programme’s select_parents_ga()/ truncation_selection() output external optimal-contribution- selection (OCS) tool. min_sel_value / min_sel_mode (new arguments, default min_sel_value = NULL = change behaviour): whole-genome merit floor applied candidate pool ranking/searching, three modes — "value" (absolute cutoff), "percentile" (keep top fraction score, self-scaling), "sd_below_mean" (cutoff expressed SDs mean, self-scaling). Without , select_parents_ga() select genuinely poor overall performers (including one strongly negative selection index) purely uniquely covered one target haplotype block — fitness function term whole-genome merit. select_parents_ga() also gains merit_score argument (named whole-genome value vector) since otherwise input evaluate floor ; value_matrix alone per-block, genome-wide. n_reps (new argument select_parents_ga(), default 5L, implicitly 1): runs n_reps independent GA replicates deterministically-derived seeds returns best-fitness one, plus new $stability list reporting per-individual selection frequency across replicates fitness range observed — single fixed-seed GA run gives information whether answer robust optimum one several near-equally-good solutions. Set n_reps = 1 previous single-run behaviour. $converged (new return field): flags whether winning replicate’s GA stopped fitness plateaued (ga_fit@iter < maxiter) rather cut maxiter without necessarily converging. what: run_haplotype_stability(): the complete_decomposition = FALSE fix (0.3.10.9000, item 1 below) was necessary but not sufficient — second, deeper bug found and fixed
title: HapBlockR 0.3.11.9000 (development)
text: second devtools::test() run (2546 passing) showed four run_haplotype_stability() failures merge() error ('' must specify uniquely valid column'), unchanged complete_decomposition = FALSE fix. fix correct (removed real column-count mismatch) reason every block’s regression degenerate. actual cause: function’s Finlay-Wilkinson environmental index computed grand mean environment’s entire local_gebv matrix (env_means <- vapply(local_by_env, function(m) mean(.numeric(m)), ...)). every entry local_gebv (x - ploidy*p) * alpha term, mean-zero construction across individuals within single fit — general property BLUP/backsolved random-effect predictions, specific one block. env_means always approximately (0, 0, ...) regardless real -environment differences, stats::var() collapsed 1e-10 degeneracy guard every block, rows ended empty, <- .call(rbind, rows) became NULL, final merge(bk, , = "block_id", .y = TRUE) failed NULL coerces 0-row/0-column data frame block_id column merge . Substituting whole-genome kin.blup() GEBV (fit$g) instead helped either — BLUP predictions mean-zero construction reason. Fixed computing environmental index way Finlay & Wilkinson (1963) originally defined : mean observed (raw phenotype/BLUE) performance across genotypes environment, derived GEBV/local-GEBV quantity. run_haplotype_stability() now tracks pheno_env_means[env] <- mean(y[common], na.rm = TRUE) (y already pulled blues_list[[env]]) inside existing per-environment loop, now built pheno_env_means, restricted whichever environments actually made local_by_env. what: Cleanup and block-selection ergonomics (HapSelect gap-analysis, part 1)
title: HapBlockR 0.3.5.9000 (development)
text: Small, mechanical fixes plus block-selection tooling identified HapBlockR-vs-HapSelect gap analysis. None change existing default behaviour except noted. Stale “eleven C++ functions” claim fixed. README.md said src/ld_core.cpp exports eleven compiled functions; exports thirteen (compute_r2_cpp, compute_rV2_cpp, maf_filter_cpp, build_adj_matrix_cpp, col_r2_cpp, compute_r2_sparse_cpp, boundary_scan_cpp, build_hap_strings_cpp, resolve_overlap_cpp, block_snp_ranges_cpp, extract_chr_haplotypes_cpp, extract_chr_haplotypes_phased_cpp, impute_and_filter_cpp — confirmed R/RcppExports.R). mentions README.md §2 §16.1 updated full function list spelled . .Rbuildignore deduplicated. ^cran-comments\.md$ ^pkgdown$ listed twice. what: New: pluggable marker-effect models, and a complete GEBV decomposition matching HapSelect
title: HapBlockR 0.3.4.9000 (development)
text: Two changes closing gap identified HapSelect’s localGEBV/marker- effect workflow. 1. estimate_marker_effects() (new, exported) — unified “Step B” marker- effect estimator, matching flexibility HapSelect’s create_marker_effects_file() (accepts rrBLUP / BGLR / Sommer / ASReml-R). method =: "gblup" (default) — existing rrBLUP::kin.blup() supplied relationship matrix, backsolved per-SNP effects via backsolve_snp_effects() (VanRaden 2008; Tong et al. 2025). Identical run_haplotype_prediction() always done internally. "rrblup" — rrBLUP::mixed.solve() fit directly marker-effect (SNP-BLUP / ridge-regression BLUP) model (Meuwissen et al. 2001; Endelman 2011). relationship matrix backsolving step. "bayesb" / "bayesc" / "bayesa" — Bayesian variable-selection regression via BGLR::BGLR() (Perez & de los Campos 2014). Requires new BGLR Suggests dependency. (Originally shipped "bayesr"; BGLR actually implement “BayesR” model — failed runtime BGLR’s “model BayesR implemented” error first time new test suite actually run. Fixed replacing real BGLR model "bayesa" — see 0.3.9.9000 entry full story.) four methods return gebv scale (M %*% alpha, centred genotype matrix times estimated marker effects), block-importance rankings comparable across method choices. run_haplotype_prediction() gains marker_effect_method parameter (default "gblup", fully backward-compatible: solver_used remains exactly "rrBLUP" default) plus n_iter/burn_in/seed Bayesian methods. 2. compute_local_gebv() — complete decomposition (complete_decomposition = TRUE, new default). Previously, SNP covered row blocks — isolated markers dropped LD-detection time (singleton_as_block = FALSE, Big_LD()/run_Big_LD_all_chr() default), blocks min_snps — silently vanished decomposition: real, non-zero backsolved effect, effect never attributed block, rowSums(local_gebv) fell short individual’s true genome-wide GEBV. HapSelect gap: def_blocks() always keeps isolated marker one-marker haploblock rather dropping , localGEBV values complete construction. compute_local_gebv() now matches guarantee: every SNP known effect isn’t covered existing block appended “singleton” pseudo-block (block_id prefixed "singleton_", n_snps = 1, flagged via new singleton column block_importance), rowSums(local_gebv) reconstructs full backsolved GEBV regardless blocks generated. Ranking (var_scaled/important) recomputed full combined set singleton LD blocks compete scale. Set complete_decomposition = FALSE restore previous (possibly incomplete) behaviour. run_haplotype_prediction()’s n_blocks now reflects actual post-decomposition block count (LD blocks + singletons added), may exceed nrow(blocks). completeness guarantee depends geno_matrix full, unfiltered, genome-wide genotype matrix (one used derive snp_effects) rather one already subset block-member SNPs (e.g. haplotype feature matrix) — SNP dropped upstream compute_local_gebv() never column begin can’t recovered inside . compute_local_gebv() now warns detectable: snp_info’s coordinates place SNPs outside every block window, none SNPs present geno_matrix , geno_matrix almost certainly pre-filtered decomposition look complete without actually . Caveat: formula-audit fixes , none executed/tested environment changes written (R available). Run devtools::test() relying estimate_marker_effects() (especially BGLR-backed methods) new compute_local_gebv() default production.

what: Correctness: formula audit fixes across LD, diversity, prediction, and association modules
title: HapBlockR 0.3.3.9000 (development)
text: full audit every estimator implemented package (LD metrics, diversity, GEBV backsolving/local prediction, association testing, cross-population concordance) cited source (VanRaden 2008, Nei 1973, Weir & Cockerham 1984, Gao et al. simpleM 2008/2010/2011, Tong et al. 2024/2025) turned six formula-level defects. six fixed release; none change public function signatures. 1. prepare_geno(method = "rV2") — missing-genotype NA propagation (critical). V_inv_sqrt %*% geno_centered full matrix product across n individuals. single unimputed NA one genotype column silently contaminated column’s whitened values every individual (just one missing call), downstream made compute_r2_cpp() treat corrupted column monomorphic zero — silently dropping SNPs clique detection warning. Fixed mean-imputing (0 centred scale) immediately whitening. r2 path never affected (C++ kernel already mean-imputes per column cross-individual mixing). 2. compute_haplotype_diversity() scan_diversity_windows() — Shannon entropy computed nats instead bits. used natural log (log()) documented formula H' = -sum(p_i * log2(p_i)). Every reported Shannon entropy value small constant factor ln(2) ≈ 0.693. Fixed switching call sites log2(). 3. compute_local_gebv() — centering convention inconsistent backsolve_snp_effects(). backsolved per-SNP effects (alpha) defined mean-centred dosages (M = geno - 2*p), compute_local_gebv() combining genotypes scaled [0, 1] (h = G/2) via h %*% alpha + (1 - h) %*% (-alpha), inconsistent parameterisation distorts local GEBV whenever allele frequencies deviate 0.5. Fixed use centred convention backsolving step: local_GEBV = (G - 2*p) %*% alpha. 4. test_block_haplotypes() — approximated EMMAX instead implementing . function fit null REML model, subtracted estimated fixed effects polygenic BLUP (y - X*beta - u_hat) ran plain OLS remainder, without ever transforming marker columns. u_hat estimate, true random effect, leftover residual fully whitened, OLS standard errors untransformed markers account correlation structure surviving residual — weakest exactly related/structured populations machinery exists . Replaced genuine GLS/EMMAX transform: phenotype every haplotype-allele column pre-multiplied V_hat^(-1/2) (via null model’s GRM eigendecomposition, computed per trait reused every marker), transformed null design (intercept + PCs) projected via Frisch-Waugh-Lovell theorem, per-allele Wald scan per-block omnibus F-test now run fully GLS-transformed quantities correspondingly corrected degrees freedom (n_ind - ncol(X_null) - 1 per allele; n_ind - ncol(X_null) - df_lrt per block). residual-scan fallback (previous approximation) retained used, warning, null model fit, GRM eigendecomposition, transformed null-design inversion fails. Also fixed latent bug fallback path per-block omnibus test: per-allele degrees freedom hardcoded assuming single intercept (n_ind - 2, n_ind - df_lrt - 1) rather discounting full null design size, -counted degrees freedom whenever n_pcs > 0 (anti-conservative p-values Q+K setting). 5. compare_block_effects() — Cochran’s Q degrees freedom one. Q_df computed n_shared_alleles - 1, Cochran’s Q k independent per-allele effect-size comparisons k degrees freedom, k - 1 (shared common-mean estimation step consuming degree freedom , unlike single-outcome meta-analysis). Fixed Q_df = n_shared_alleles. 6. compare_haplotype_populations() — FST reduced simple allele-frequency-variance ratio instead documented Weir & Cockerham (1984) estimator. previous formula omitted finite-sample bias correction within-population heterozygosity component entirely, overstating FST small sample sizes. Replaced full three-variance- component WC1984 estimator (, b, c, n_bar, n_C, p_bar, s_squared, h_bar), verified well-established reference implementation (scikit-allel). also fixed previously unflagged latent bug: phased "gamete1|gamete2" diplotype strings never split individual alleles frequency/FST computation, phased-data FST silently computed diplotype combinations rather true allele frequencies. Unphased data (heterozygosity component available) falls back h_bar = 0, equivalent treating data haploid, . Caveat: formula-level corrections verified manual derivation cross-referencing cited literature , FST, external reference implementation. Run devtools::test() / R CMD check relying results computed version, particularly test_block_haplotypes().

title: HapBlockR 0.3.2.9000 (development)
text: Three new exported functions implement within-block -block epistasis detection. operate GRM-corrected REML residuals null model test_block_haplotypes(), ensuring population-structure-corrected tests throughout. scan_block_epistasis() — Within-block pairwise SNP epistasis scan. Tests C(p, 2) SNP pairs within significant blocks interaction term aa_ij y = mu + ai*xi + aj*xj + aa_ij*(xi*xj) + e. Restricted significant blocks (controlled sig_blocks) avoid genome-wide combinatorial explosion. Multiple-testing correction: Bonferroni simpleM Sidak within block; Meff estimated eigenspectrum pairwise interaction column matrix. sig_metric parameter (default "p_simplem_sidak") controls correction drives significant flag. Output columns: p_wald, p_bonf, p_simplem, p_simplem_sidak, Meff, significant, significant_bonf, significant_simplem, significant_simplem_sidak. Returns HapBlockR_epistasis. scan_block_by_block_epistasis() — Trans-haplotype -block epistasis scan. Tests significant haplotype alleles every allele blocks: O(n_sig × n_total_alleles) tests, Bonferroni corrected. Identifies genetic background dependence resistance haplotype one locus functions presence specific background another locus — form epistasis single-block single-SNP analyses detect. 25 significant alleles × 17,943 total alleles scan involves ~450,000 tests. Returns HapBlockR_block_epistasis. fine_map_epistasis_block() — Single-block epistasis fine-mapping. Identifies specific interacting SNP pairs within one block. Dispatches exhaustive pairwise scan blocks p ≤ 200 SNPs (method = "pairwise"), LASSO pairwise interaction terms via glmnet::cv.glmnet() lambda.1se larger blocks (method = "lasso"). method = "auto" (default) selects automatically. Requires pre-computed REML residuals (y_resid). Shared internal helpers added: .fit_null_reml(), .pairwise_interaction_scan(). glmnet added Suggests (required fine_map_epistasis_block(method = "lasso")). 43 new tests tests/testthat/test-epistasis.R.

what: Enhancement: PC model selection and expanded plot outputs in test_block_haplotypes()
title: HapBlockR 0.3.1.9000 (development)
text: test_block_haplotypes() now supports automatic selection number population structure covariates (n_pcs) via new BIC/lambda/hybrid optimisation framework, produces three new diagnostic plots PDF format. New parameters: optimize_pcs = FALSE — TRUE, fits REML null models n_pcs = 0..optimize_pcs_max selects value minimising score criterion chosen optimize_method. Uses first trait (GRM shared across traits). FALSE (default), n_pcs used directly. optimize_pcs_max = 10L — upper bound number PCs evaluated optimisation. "bic" — minimise BIC null REML model: −2·logLik + k·log(n), k = intercept + n_pcs + σ²_g + σ²_e. "lambda" — minimise |λ_GC − 1|, λ estimated fast 500-allele scan GRM-corrected residuals. directly targets genomic control calibration. "bic_lambda" (default, recommended GWAS) — hybrid score: |λ − 1| + 0.01 × scaled_BIC. Minimises inflation/deflation BIC breaks ties toward simpler (fewer PCs) model. New return element: $pc_model_selection — data.frame one row per k tested: n_pcs, BIC, lambda_gc, score, selected. Printed print() visible run log. NULL optimize_pcs = FALSE. Plot changes (breaking): plots now saved PDF instead PNG. Three plots produced per run: manhattan_<trait>.pdf — unchanged content, format changed PDF. qq_<trait>.pdf — unchanged content, format changed PDF. pca_grm.pdf — new: individuals PC1 × PC2 space (GRM eigenvectors), coloured first trait’s phenotype using blue-white-red diverging palette. Subtitle reports number PCs used model. grm_scree.pdf — new: scree plot GRM eigenvalues (PC30), selected PC cutoff highlighted red cumulative variance curve overlaid dashed line. optimize_pcs = TRUE, subtitle reports selection criterion, selected k, lambda_GC. Breaking change note: downstream code expected manhattan_*.png qq_*.png file names must updated use .pdf extension.

what: Enhancement: full multiple-testing correction set in estimate_diplotype_effects()
title: HapBlockR 0.3.1.9000 (development)
text: estimate_diplotype_effects() now computes four correction columns test_block_haplotypes(), making two modules symmetric. significant flag now driven user-selected criterion rather always using plain Bonferroni. New parameters: sig_threshold = 0.05 — significance cutoff applied p-value selected sig_metric. "p_omnibus_adj" — plain Bonferroni × n_blocks_per_trait (old default, retained backward compatibility). "p_omnibus_fdr" — Benjamini-Hochberg FDR. "p_omnibus_simplem" — simpleM Bonferroni-style: min(p × Meff, 1), Meff estimated block-summary PC1 eigenspectrum. what: Enhancement: simpleM multiple-testing correction in test_block_haplotypes()
title: HapBlockR 0.3.1.9000 (development)
text: test_block_haplotypes() now implements simpleM procedure (Gao et al. 2008, 2010, 2011) LD-aware multiple-testing correction correlated haplotype allele tests. simpleM estimates effective number independent tests (Meff) eigenspectrum haplotype allele dosage correlation matrix, replacing raw test counting LD-aware effective count less conservative Bonferroni providing family-wise error control. what: Haplotype association testing and breeding decision functions
title: HapBlockR 0.3.1 (development)
text: Four new exported functions complete statistical inference breeding decision layer. Haplotype association testing test_block_haplotypes(haplotypes, blues, blocks, n_pcs, top_n, min_freq,   id_col, blue_col, blue_cols, alpha, verbose) — Block-level haplotype association tests via unified Q+K mixed linear model (EMMAX/GAPIT3 formulation): y = mu + alpha·x_hap + sum(beta_k·PC_k) + g + e, PC_k GRM-derived eigenvectors (fixed effects population structure) g ~ MVN(0, sigma_g^2 G) polygenic kinship random effect. GRM inverted per trait via rrBLUP::mixed.solve() (O(n^3)); per-allele scan across blocks fully vectorised single crossprod() call (O(n*p), BLAS trick marginal SNP screening). Returns HapBlockR_haplotype_assoc object $allele_tests (per-allele Wald tests: effect, SE, t, p_wald, p_wald_adj, significant) $block_tests (omnibus F-test per block: F_stat, p_omnibus, p_omnibus_adj, var_explained, significant_omnibus). n_pcs = 0L (default): EMMAX pure GRM; n_pcs > 0: Q+K model; n_pcs = NULL: auto-select via scree elbow. estimate_diplotype_effects(haplotypes, blues, blocks, min_freq,   min_n_diplotype, id_col, blue_col, blue_cols, verbose) — Estimates additive dominance effects diplotype class means LD block, GRM kinship correction. allele pair (, B): additive effect = (mean_BB - mean_AA) / 2; dominance deviation d = mean_AB - midpoint; dominance ratio d/(0 = additive, +/-1 = complete dominance, |d/| > 1 = overdominance). Returns HapBlockR_diplotype object $diplotype_means, $dominance_table (, d, d_over_a, overdominance per allele pair per block per trait), $omnibus_tests (F-test per block). Breeding decision tools score_favorable_haplotypes(haplotypes, allele_effects, min_freq,   missing_string, normalize) — Scores individual’s genome-wide haplotype portfolio table known per-allele effects. Block score = sum(allele_effect × dosage) per block. Genome-wide stacking index = sum across scored blocks, normalised [0,1] normalize = TRUE. Returns ranked data frame (one row per individual) stacking_index, n_blocks_scored, mean_block_score, rank, one score_<block_id> column per scored block detailed inspection. summarize_parent_haplotypes(haplotypes, candidate_ids, allele_effects,   blocks, min_freq, missing_string) — Produces tidy long-format allele inventory (one row per individual × block × allele) candidate parents. Reports allele dosage (0/1 unphased; 0/1/2 phased), population allele frequency, optional allele effect, is_rare flag (freq < 0.10). Includes rows dosage = 0 candidates can compared rows. Primary tool identifying complementary rare alleles across candidates designing haplotype stacking crosses.

title: HapBlockR 0.3.1 (development)
text: Ten new exported functions extend pipeline without modifying existing function. two new files: R/analysis_extensions.R R/haplotype_inference.R. Cross-validation model evaluation cv_haplotype_prediction() — k-fold cross-validation haplotype GBLUP model. Masks phenotypes fold--fold, predicts via rrBLUP::kin.blup() using shared haplotype GRM, returns predictive ability (Pearson r) RMSE per trait per fold. Supports multiple replications multiple traits. Returns HapBlockR_cv object pa_summary, pa_mean, k, n_rep. Population comparison compare_haplotype_populations() — computes Weir-Cockerham (1984) FST allele frequency differences per block two named sample groups. Returns FST, max_freq_diff, dominant allele per group, chi-squared p-value (Monte Carlo, B=2000), divergent flag (FST > 0.1 p < 0.05). Suitable breeding cycle monitoring wild/elite panel comparisons. Visualisation plot_haplotype_network() — draws minimum-spanning network haplotype alleles within one LD block using igraph::mst() Hamming-distance edge weights. Node size proportional frequency. Optional group colouring via groups named vector. Returns igraph MST object invisibly. Multi-environment stability run_haplotype_stability() — Finlay-Wilkinson (1963) regression per-block local GEBV contributions environmental index across environments. Returns slope b (stability coefficient), SE, R², deviation mean square s²d, stable flag (H0: b=1 rejected alpha=0.05). Requires least 2 environments. Annotation export export_candidate_regions() — converts define_qtl_regions() output BED (0-based, UCSC/BEDtools-compatible), CSV, named list ready biomaRt::getBM(). Supports chr_prefix, LD-extended windows via use_lead_snp, padding_bp. Effect decomposition decompose_block_effects() — aggregates per-SNP additive effects (backsolve_snp_effects()) per-haplotype-allele effect table. Effect = sum(SNP_effect × allele_dosage) per allele position. Returns allele_effect, effect_rank, frequency per allele per block. Directly links prediction model output selection index construction. Genome-wide diversity scanning scan_diversity_windows() — sliding-window / Shannon / n_eff_alleles scan across genome independent LD block boundaries. Window size step controlled window_bp step_bp. Returns data frame one row per window including sweep_flag (freq_dominant >= 0.90). True haplotype inference harmonisation infer_block_haplotypes() — converts raw haplotype strings structured per-individual, per-block diplotype table explicit hap1, hap2, diplotype (canonical sorted string), heterozygous, phase_ambiguous, missing columns. Handles phased input (read_phased_vcf(), phase_ambiguous always FALSE) unphased input (heterozygous genotypes set phase_ambiguous = TRUE unless resolve_unphased = TRUE triggers maximum-parsimony heuristic). collapse_haplotypes() — merges rare haplotype alleles (min_freq) biologically meaningful groups rather dropping . Three strategies: "rare_to_other" (pool <>), "nearest" (merge similar common allele Hamming distance), "tree_based" (UPGMA dendrogram; merges rare alleles coarsest cut avoids merging common alleles ). Preserves label_map attribute recording every original→collapsed mapping use harmonize_haplotypes(). harmonize_haplotypes() — makes haplotype allele labels transferable across training/validation splits, populations, environments. Builds reference dictionary alleles min_freq_ref reference panel; matches target alleles exact string first, nearest Hamming neighbour (max_hamming), labels unmatched alleles "<novel>". Attaches harmonization_report attribute reporting n_exact, n_nearest, n_novel, mean_hamming_dist per block.

title: HapBlockR 0.3.1 (development)
text: compute_ld_decay() — LD decay analysis per chromosome. Estimates distance r² (rV²) drops critical threshold using memory-efficient position-first random sampling strategy: pair indices sampled SNP positions , read_chunk() loads unique SNP columns involved (~2% WGS chromosome 50k random pairs). compute_r2_sparse_cpp() (Armadillo BLAS + OpenMP) called per chromosome place R pair--pair loop. Two threshold approaches: fixed numeric (e.g. 0.1, standard GWAS practice) parametric (95th percentile r² unlinked markers different chromosomes, measuring background kinship-induced LD level). Optional LOESS Hill-Weir (1988) nonlinear decay model fitting. Chromosome-specific decay distances can passed directly define_qtl_regions(ld_decay = decay) define biologically justified candidate gene windows. Censored distances (threshold never crossed within max_dist) flagged censored = TRUE output emitted warnings. Requires change existing code. plot_ld_decay() — ggplot2 visualisation r² vs physical distance per chromosome, optional raw points, threshold line, per-chromosome decay distance markers, facet option.

title: HapBlockR 0.3.1 (development)
text: LD-informed overlap resolution replacing blind union merge Big_LD(). Overlapping blocks sub-segment seams now resolved cumulative-score boundary rule: disputed SNP, score = mean_r2(left core) -   mean_r2(right core). cumulative sum tracked across overlap zone split boundary placed last position cumulative score >= 0. Representatives selected boundary-adjacent SNPs core (nearest overlap zone, first-k). Three clean cases: -left (block keeps overlap, block B shrinks), -right (block shrinks, block B keeps overlap), mixed (split cumulative boundary). Falls back union merge one core empty (one block fully inside ).

title: HapBlockR 0.3.1 (development)

title: HapBlockR 0.3.1 (development)
text: compute_ld_decay() pair sampling — snp_info now sorted POS within chromosome pair index sampling. Previously, unsorted input produce incorrect pair distances silently. compute_ld_decay() column precomputation — prepared columns (mean-imputed, optionally whitened) now computed per chunk, per pair. Monomorphic columns (sd < 1e-6 preparation) skipped r² computation. compute_ld_decay() mode — sliding-window random pairs now kept separate: sliding window feeds decay curve, random pairs feed parametric threshold . Previously merged one pool, biasing curve shape estimate. compute_ld_decay() fitting failures — LOESS Hill-Weir nonlinear failures now emit warning() chromosome name error message instead silently swallowed tryCatch(..., error = function(e) NULL). compute_ld_decay() threshold crossing — linear interpolation last-first-bins sub-bin precision (: first-bin midpoint). Non-monotone curves fall back first-. r2_threshold validation — numeric thresholds outside [0,1], NA values, unrecognised strings now produce informative errors instead silent wrong results.

title: HapBlockR 0.3.1 (development)
text: extract_haplotypes() C++ optimisation — haplotype strings now built via build_hap_strings_cpp(), replacing R vapply() loop incurred one function call per individual per block. 3M-SNP panel 17,078 blocks 204 individuals: ~3.5 million R calls -> one C++ call per block. Expected speedup: 20-50x (3.5 hours -> ~5-10 minutes panel). read_chunk() bigmemory NA fix — char-type big.matrix stores NA -128; now correctly restored NA_integer_. Also removed redundant integer->double type conversion.

title: HapBlockR 0.3.1 (development)
text: Louvain/Leiden community detection (CLQmode = "Louvain" "Leiden"): Polynomial-time O(n log n) community detection replaces Bron-Kerbosch (igraph::max_cliques()) exponential worst-case complexity. original Big-LD run 3M-SNP WGS panel found 4.26 million maximal cliques single 1500-SNP window ran > 1 hour without completing. Louvain/Leiden finish window < 1 second. Block boundaries equivalent better Density mode WGS panels LD structure dense. Available CLQD(), Big_LD(), run_Big_LD_all_chr(), tune_LD_params(), run_ldx_pipeline(). Edge weights inversely proportional base-pair distance local LD structure respected. Sparse LD computation (max_bp_distance parameter): max_bp_distance > 0, SNP pairs within physical distance r² computed via compute_r2_sparse_cpp(). Pairs beyond threshold assumed negligible LD set zero adjacency matrix. reduces O(p²) LD computation near-O(p) WGS panels — 500 kb, approximately 70–90% pairs skipped. Available CLQD(), propagated callers. Default 0L (disabled) preserves original behaviour. Memory-mapped genotype store (read_geno_bigmemory()): Wraps genotype source bigmemory::big.matrix backed binary file disk. read_chunk() retrieves columns via OS page faults — requested bytes loaded RAM. Peak RAM proportional n_samples × subSegmSize × 8 bytes, full genome matrix. Backing files persist across R sessions: supply .desc path reattach without re-loading source data. Storage type "char" (1 byte per cell) saves 8× RAM vs double 0/1/2 dosage values. Requires bigmemory (added Suggests).

title: HapBlockR 0.3.0
text: read_phased_vcf(): read pre-phased VCF 0|1 GT fields; returns hap1/hap2 gamete matrices plus combined dosage. phase_with_beagle(): call Beagle 5.x statistical phasing WGS data; returns path phased VCF.gz. unphase_to_dosage(): collapse phased gamete matrices back 0/1/2 (internal helper; exported). Auto-detects phased vs unphased input list structure. Unphased mode: diploid string "012201" per individual per block. Phased mode: two-gamete string "011|100" per individual per block. Blocks strictly per-chromosome; cross-chromosome blocks architecturally impossible. n_eff_alleles: effective number alleles = 1/Σpᵢ² (Hill 1973), ranging 1 (monomorphic) k (equal frequencies). sweep_flag: TRUE freq_dominant ≥ 0.90, flagging possible selective sweeps strong founder effects (Difabachew et al. 2023). now sample-size corrected following Nei (1973): = n/(n-1) × (1 − Σpᵢ²). Output now includes CHR, start_bp, end_bp, n_snps columns direct use genomic region analyses. Converts raw dosage strings (e.g. "02110") nucleotide sequences (e.g. "AGTTA") using REF/ALT snp_info. Returns data frame: block_id, CHR, start_bp, end_bp, hap_rank, hap_id, dosage_string, nucleotide_sequence, frequency, n_carriers, snp_positions, snp_alleles. New encoding = parameter: "additive_012" (default) "presence_01". Phased + "additive_012": true 0/1/2 allele counts per gamete (0=absent, 1=one gamete, 2=gametes). Unphased + "additive_012": 0/1/NA — 1=present, 0=absent. value 2 used homozygosity inferred unphased strings. "presence_01": 0/1 presence/absence kernel methods random forests (formerly "presence_02"; "presence_02" accepted backward-compat alias). New min_freq = parameter drop rare haplotype allele columns. top_n default changed 5L NULL (retain alleles min_freq). Maps significant GWAS markers onto LD blocks post-GWAS. Flags pleiotropic blocks (significant hits multiple traits). Implements haploblock-based QTL cataloguing approach Tong et al. (2024) Theoretical Applied Genetics 137:274. Now accepts optional BETA column gwas_results. supplied, output includes: lead_beta (effect lead SNP), sig_snps (significant SNP IDs, semicolon-separated), sig_betas (marginal effects). See ?define_qtl_regions block effect estimation approaches. write_haplotype_numeric(): tab-delimited dosage matrix (0/1/2/NA). Metadata column alleles shows nucleotide sequence allele. Compatible rrBLUP, BGLR, ASReml-R. write_haplotype_character(): tab-delimited nucleotide matrix. cell shows nucleotide sequence individual carries allele, "-" absent, "." missing. Heterozygous SNP positions encoded IUPAC ambiguity codes (R=/G, Y=C/T, S=G/C, W=/T, K=G/T, M=/C), keeping sequence length n_snps. Alleles column shows REF/ALT every block SNP (semicolon-separated). write_haplotype_diversity(): CSV per-block diversity metrics optional genome-wide mean summary row. write_haplotype_hapmap() removed. diploid AA//TT HapMap encoding meaningful multi-SNP haplotype alleles. Haplotype string decoder (decode_haplotype_strings()): exported function mapping dosage strings nucleotide sequences full SNP-level metadata. Extends run_haplotype_prediction() k traits simultaneously. One trait-agnostic GRM (computed ) shared across traits. GBLUP solver: attempts sommer::mmer() multi-trait model first; automatically falls back rrBLUP::kin.blup() per-trait loop sommer installed model fails converge. Block importance aggregated across traits: var_scaled_mean, n_traits_important, important_any, important_all per block. importance_rule argument controls combined flag: '' (≥ 1 trait), '' (traits), 'mean' (mean ≥ 0.9). blues accepts wide data frame (one column per trait) named list named numeric vectors (different individuals per trait). sommer added Suggests; rrBLUP required fallback. run_haplotype_prediction_mt() removed; functionality fully absorbed unified run_haplotype_prediction() API. Cites Covarrubias-Pazaran (2016) sommer Endelman (2011) rrBLUP. compute_haplotype_grm(): VanRaden (2008) GRM haplotype feature matrix. Mean-imputes NA, clamps frequencies, returns symmetric n×n matrix. backsolve_snp_effects(): derives per-SNP additive effects GEBV without refitting marker model: α̂ = M′G⁻¹ĝ / 2Σp(1−p) (Tong et al. 2025 Theor Appl Genet 138:267). compute_local_gebv(): local haplotype GEBV per block = sum SNP effects within block. Ranks blocks Var(local GEBV); important flag scaled variance ≥ 0.90 (Tong et al. 2024 Theor Appl Genet 137:274). prepare_gblup_inputs(): aligns haplotype feature matrix phenotype data frame; computes returns bended GRM ready rrBLUP, sommer, ASReml-R, BGLR. run_haplotype_prediction(): end--end Tong et al. (2024/2025) pipeline pre-adjusted phenotype values (BLUEs/BLUPs) block importance. Accepts blues named numeric vector data frame id_col blue_col arguments. Uses rrBLUP::kin.blup() REML-based GBLUP. Returns standard pipeline outputs plus GEBV, per-SNP effects, local haplotype GEBV matrix, block importance table. integrate_gwas_haplotypes(): combines GWAS evidence (has_gwas_hit), variance evidence (is_important, scaled Var(local GEBV) ≥ 0.9), diversity evidence (is_diverse, ≥ threshold) priority_score (0–3) plain-language recommendation per block. diversity-— rank ; (2) GWAS-— binary GWAS-hit flag tiebreaker, p-value used ranking; (3) phenotype — rank scaled Var(local GEBV). Returns standard pipeline outputs plus ranked_blocks data frame. hap_format = "hapmap" renamed hap_format = "character". Big_LD arguments now exposed: clstgap, split, appendrare, singleton_as_block, checkLargest, digits, kin_method, CLQmode. Previously 8 silently using Big_LD defaults. min_freq parameter exposed (previously hardcoded inside build_haplotype_feature_matrix). Return list now includes geno_matrix (individuals × SNPs, MAF-filtered), enabling direct use tune_LD_params() run_haplotype_prediction() without reloading genotype file. tune_LD_params() default grid now jointly optimises CLQcut (4 values) min_freq (2 values), giving 8 combinations. Weber et al. (2023) show hyperparameters requiring dataset-specific tuning.

title: HapBlockR 0.3.0
text: Multi-format /O: read_geno() supports numeric dosage CSV, HapMap, VCF / bgzipped VCF, SNPRelate GDS, PLINK BED/BIM/FAM, plain R matrices. SNPRelate GDS streaming backend: peak RAM proportional one window. Replaces previous SeqArray backend entirely. PLINK BED backend: BEDMatrix-backed memory-mapped access. read_chunk(), close_backend(): unified accessor interface. run_Big_LD_all_chr() accepts HapBlockR_backend directly. min_snps_chr parameter: skip scaffolds fewer SNPs (default 10). clean_malformed parameter read_geno(), run_Big_LD_all_chr(), run_ldx_pipeline(): streams input files remove malformed lines GDS conversion (NGSEP GATK-origin VCFs). chr parameter run_Big_LD_all_chr() run_ldx_pipeline(): restrict processing specific chromosomes. ldx_gwas example dataset now includes trait column ("TraitA" / "TraitB") demonstrate multi-trait pleiotropic block detection via define_qtl_regions(trait_col = "trait").

title: HapBlockR 0.3.0
text: boundary_scan_cpp(): C++ boundary scan replaces R inner loop (~20x faster). maf_filter_cpp(): combined MAF + monomorphic filter, single O(np) pass (~10x faster panels > 100 k SNPs). build_adj_matrix_cpp(): -place adjacency construction, eliminates intermediate allocation. compute_r2_sparse_cpp(): sparse r² within bp window, avoids O(p²) cost large sub-segments.

title: HapBlockR 0.3.0
text: Chunked pre-allocated numeric CSV reader: two-pass strategy — header scan Pass 1, fixed 50,000-row chunks fill single pre-allocated matrix Pass 2. Peak RAM = one chunk, 2x file. VCF HapMap mandatory SNPRelate GDS auto-conversion: transparent streaming GDS backend first call; cache reused subsequent calls. Explicit per-chromosome gc() run_Big_LD_all_chr() extract_haplotypes(): prevents heap fragmentation across 20-30 chromosome passes.

title: HapBlockR 0.3.0
text: test-ld-decay.R: 33 tests compute_ld_decay() plot_ld_decay() covering: input validation, HapBlockR_decay object structure, sampling modes, unsorted snp_info handling, threshold types (fixed, parametric, , NULL), fit_model options, decay distance correctness, censored flag, three backend types (matrix, HapBlockR_backend, bigmemory), print plot methods, define_qtl_regions() integration ld_decay=. test-basic.R: smoke tests covering major functions via 230-SNP example dataset (3 chromosomes, 9 LD blocks). test-algorithm.R: property-based tests Big-LD segmentation algorithm: CLQD, Big_LD, run_Big_LD_all_chr, summarise_blocks, plot_ld_blocks. test-haplotypes.R: comprehensive tests haplotype extraction (phased unphased), diversity metrics (n_eff_alleles, sweep_flag), QTL region definition (lead_beta, sig_snps, sig_betas), feature matrix encoding (additive_012 / presence_01), output writers, rank_haplotype_blocks, integrate_gwas_haplotypes.
